The '''2025–26 season''' was [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal Football Club]]'s 34th season in the [[Premier League]], their [[List of Arsenal F.C. seasons|100th consecutive season]] in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of English football, becoming the first team to spend 100 seasons straight in the English top flight, and 109th season in the top flight overall.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |title=All-time Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=18 Jun 2013 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 May 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622042610/https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |archive-date=22 Jun 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |title=English Clubs Divisional Movements 1888–2016 |last1=Ross |first1=James |last2=Heneghan |first2=Michael |last3=Orford |first3=Stuart |last4=Culliton |first4=Eoin |date=25 Aug 2016 |website=[[RSSSF|Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |access-date=5 May 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622041929/https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |archive-date=22 Jun 2023}}</ref> In addition to the [[2025–26 Premier League|domestic league]], Arsenal also participated in the [[2025–26 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2025–26 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], the latter of which was their [[Arsenal F.C. in European football|40th European campaign]]. The season covers the period from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026.

On 19 May 2026, Arsenal were crowned as Premier League champions with a game left to play after title rivals [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] drew 1–1 to [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], resulting in Arsenal's first league title since the [[2003–04 Arsenal F.C. season|2003–04 Invincible season]] and 14th title overall (4th in the [[Premier League]] era).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://espn.com/football/story/_/id/48813813/arsenal-win-premier-league-title-2026-manchester-city-bournemouth |title=Arsenal win 1st Premier League title in 22 years after Man City draw |publisher=ESPN |date=19 May 2026 }}</ref> The club officially celebrated their title triumph after their concluding match victory against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on 24 May.

==Review==
===Background===
{{See also|2024–25 Arsenal F.C. season}}

Arsenal's 2024–25 campaign was heavily affected by injuries and suspensions.<ref name="2024–25 season NYT 1">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6094434/2025/01/29/arsenals-list-of-misfortunes-is-long-enough-to-derail-a-season-and-yet/ |title=Arsenal's list of misfortunes is long enough to derail a season. And yet... |last=McNicholas |first=James |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6336920/2025/05/26/arsenal-review-of-2024-25/ |title=Arsenal review of 2024–25: The rise of Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri, beating Real, but a season of what-ifs |last=de Roché |first=Art |date=26 May 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref><ref name="2024–25 season ESPN">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45348059/story-arsenals-season-did-not-signing-striker-cost-them |title=Story of Arsenal's season: Did not signing striker cost them? |last=Olley |first=James |date=28 May 2025 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref> The club did not sign any player in the winter transfer window, after sporting director [[Edu Gaspar]] suddenly resigned midway through the season.<ref name="2024–25 season NYT 1"/><ref name="2024–25 season ESPN"/>

The Gunners won twenty Premier League games in 2024–25, which was eight less than the previous campaign. They dropped 21 points from winning positions in the competition that season, their joint-worst record in a single campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704619 |title=Bournemouth fight back to seal first-ever win at Arsenal |date=3 May 2025 |website=ESPN |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref> Arsenal lost four Premier League matches that campaign – one less than the previous season. That represented their lowest loss total in a top-flight campaign since [[2007–08 Arsenal F.C. season|2007–08]].<ref name="season stats AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/games-goals-great-stats-numbers-behind-2425 |title=Games, goals, great stats: Numbers behind 24/25 |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=29 May 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref> For a second consecutive season, they held the division's best defensive record, conceding a league-low 34 times.<ref name="season stats AFC"/> Arteta's side finished as Premier League runners-up for the third consecutive campaign, becoming the first club to achieve this twice in English top flight history after also doing so between 1999 and 2001. [[Kai Havertz]] finished the season as the Gunners' top scorer in the league with nine goals.
It was the first time in 101 years since the [[1923–24 Arsenal F. C. season|1923–24]] season in which Arsenal did not have a player score at least 10 league goals.

Arsenal started their 21st Champions League season since [[1992–93 UEFA Champions League|1992–93]] in September 2024. They finished third in the league phase in January 2025 and bypassed February's play-off round to go straight to the last 16.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/girona-vs-arsenal/report/521733 |title=Girona 1–2 Arsenal: Ethan Nwaneri scores on first Champions League start as Gunners seal last-16 spot |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=[[Sky Sports]] |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref> The Gunners completed a 5–1 aggregate triumph over the reigning Champions League champions [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the quarter-finals, reaching the semi-finals of the competition for the first time since [[2008–09 Arsenal F.C. season|2008–09]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2025/04/real-madrid-vs-arsenal-stats-opta-champions-league |title=Real Madrid 1–2 Arsenal Stats (1–5 agg): Arsenal Sleek, Madrid Meek as Gunners Seal Memorable Victory Over European Giants |last=Furniss |first=Matt |date=16 Apr 2025 |website=The Analyst |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref> After a 3–1 aggregate loss to French side [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], Arteta's side were eliminated from the Champions League at the semi-final stage.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-May-07/paris-saint-germain-fc-2-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Paris Saint-Germain 2–1 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=7 May 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref>

===Pre-season===
On 6 June and 26 June respectively, the club announced new long-term contracts for Brazilian defender [[Gabriel Magalhães]]<ref name="Magalhães new contract AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-signs?ĺk-new-arsenal-contract |title=Gabriel signs new Arsenal contract |date=6 Jun 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=6 Jun 2025}}</ref><ref name="Magalhães new contract BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cq691rm32n7o |title=Gabriel signs new Arsenal deal until 2029 |last=Brotherton |first=Alex |date=6 Jun 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=6 Jun 2025}}</ref> and [[Arsenal F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Academy]] graduate [[Myles Lewis-Skelly]].<ref name="Lewis-Skelly new contract AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/myles-lewis-skelly-signs-new-contract |title=Myles Lewis-Skelly signs new contract |date=26 Jun 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=26 Jun 2025}}</ref><ref name="Lewis-Skelly new contract BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/czdvnezp6g9o |title=Lewis-Skelly signs new five-year Arsenal deal |last=Jackon |first=Bobbie |date=26 Jun 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=26 Jun 2025}}</ref> Gabriel, at the time of signing the contract, was the leading Premier League goalscorer amongst defenders since his debut in 2020;<ref name="Magalhães new contract AFC"/> Lewis-Skelly enjoyed a breakthrough season, becoming the youngest starter for the club in the [[UEFA Champions League]] for 13 years.<ref name="Lewis-Skelly new contract AFC"/> On 8 August, Arsenal announced the long-term contract renewal of another Academy graduate in [[Ethan Nwaneri]]. At the time of his renewal, he remained Arsenal's youngest ever appearance maker at the age of 15 years and 181 days and left a big impression on the first team last season with nine goals in all competitions.<ref name="Nwaneri new contract AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/ethan-nwaneri-signs-new-contract |title=Ethan Nwaneri signs new contract |date=8 Aug 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=8 Aug 2025}}</ref><ref name="Nwaneri new contract BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c36j5g8r2z0o |title=Nwaneri signs new long-term Arsenal deal |last=Sutcliffe |first=Steve |date=8 Aug 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=8 Aug 2025}}</ref>

On 8 July, Arsenal announced the appointment of former Argentinian defender [[Gabriel Heinze]] as a first team assistant coach,<ref name="Heinze appointed AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-heinze-joins-coaching-team |title=Gabriel Heinze joins coaching team |date=8 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=8 Jul 2025}}</ref> replacing [[Carlos Cuesta (football manager)|Carlos Cuesta]] who departed the club to become the Head Coach of [[Serie A]] side [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] on 19 June.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.parmacalcio1913.com/news/carlos-cuesta-e-lallenatore-del-parma-calcio/ |title=Carlos Cuesta è l'allenatore del Parma Calcio |date=19 Jun 2025 |website=Parma Calcio 1913 |access-date=8 Jul 2025 |language=it |trans-title=Carlos Cuesta is the coach of Parma Calcio}}</ref> Heinze and Arteta were previously teammates at [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the [[2001–02 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|2001–02]] season.<ref name="Heinze appointed NYTimes">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6478034/2025/07/08/arsenal-heinze-coach-appointment/ |title=Arsenal appoint Gabriel Heinze to join Mikel Arteta's coaching staff |last=Onyeagwara |first=Nnamdi |date=8 Jul 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=8 Jul 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal took part in the Singapore Festival of Football between 23 and 27 July, which consisted of matches against European heavyweights [[AC Milan]] and fellow Premier League side [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in the [[National Stadium, Singapore|National Stadium]] of [[Singapore]]. Against the [[Serie A|Italian]] side a first-time cross from [[Jakub Kiwior]], that was tapped in at the back post by [[Bukayo Saka]] 8 minutes into the second half, was enough to secure a narrow 1–0 win. In the subsequent mandatory [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], three saves from debutant Kepa were not enough to stop Arsenal losing the shootout 6–5, with misses from captain [[Martin Ødegaard]], [[Reiss Nelson]], Kiwior and academy centre-back Marli Salmon.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jul-23/arsenal-1-0-ac-milan-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1-0 AC Milan |last=James |first=Josh |date=23 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=27 Jul 2025}}</ref> ''The Gunners'' then made it back-to-back wins as they ran out as 3–2 victors over Newcastle United. A goal from [[Mikel Merino]] and an [[Own goal#Association football|own goal]] from [[Alex Murphy (footballer)|Alex Murphy]] two minutes later, overturned a 6th-minute opener from [[Anthony Elanga]] inside the first 35 minutes of the match. A shot from distance was enough for [[Jacob Murphy]] to draw the [[Tyneside]] club level partway through the second half, before a powerful run from 15-year-old [[Max Dowman]] drew a penalty for a push from [[Joelinton]]. Ødegaard made no mistake from the spot 6 minutes from time and sealed the one-goal victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jul-27/arsenal-3-2-newcastle-united-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-2 Newcastle United |last=James |first=Josh |date=27 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=27 Jul 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal's Asian Tour then saw the squad travel to Hong Kong to play the first [[North London derby]] outside of the [[United Kingdom|UK]] in the history of the rivalry.<ref name="First foreign NLD">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c2deg950wnko |title=Arsenal to meet Tottenham in first game outside of UK |date=31 Mar 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref> On the stroke of half-time, Lewis-Skelly was dispossessed by [[Pape Matar Sarr]] in a crowded midfield. [[David Raya]], who had played the initial pass to Lewis-Skelly, was consequently caught high up the pitch, thus allowing Sarr to execute a well-taken long-range lob.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jul-31/arsenal-0-1-tottenham-hotspur-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 0-1 Tottenham Hotspur |last=James |first=Josh |date=31 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2 Aug 2025}}</ref> Despite taking 16 shots on the night, Arsenal were unable to overturn the deficit as Tottenham secured the 1–0 victory, thus condemning ''The Gunners'' to their first loss of pre-season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cx2xn0gyypdo |title=What we learned as Spurs beat Arsenal in Hong Kong |last=Howell |first=Alex |date=31 Jul 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 Aug 2025}}</ref>

The club's pre-season schedule was then rounded off with two [[Emirates Stadium|home]] friendlies against [[La Liga|Spanish]] sides [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] and [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref name="Villarreal and Bilbao Friendlies">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/villarreal-and-athletic-club-friendlies-confirmed |title=Villarreal and Athletic Club friendlies confirmed |date=5 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 Jul 2025}}</ref> The first of these friendlies resulted in a second consecutive single-goal loss as goals from [[Christian Nørgaard]], his first for the club, and Ødegaard from the spot, following another penalty-earning action from Dowman, were not enough to overturn the deficit created by goals from former Gunner [[Nicolas Pépé]], youngster [[Karl Etta Eyong]] and former North London rival [[Arnaut Danjuma]]. Following their 3–2 win, ''The Yellow Submarine'' also ran out 4–3 winners in the subsequent penalty shoot-out, as despite yet another shoot-out save from Kepa, misses from Merino, Gabriel Magalhães and debutant Madueke proved crucial.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Aug-06/arsenal-2-3-villarreal-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2-3 Villarreal |last=James |first=Josh |date=6 Aug 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=8 Aug 2025}}</ref> The [[Emirates Cup]] fixture against Athletic Bilbao, which occurred eight days before the club's Premier League opener at [[Old Trafford]], then resulted in ''The Gunners'' running out as comfortable 3–0 winners.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Aug-09/arsenal-3-0-athletic-club-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-0 Athletic Club |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=9 Aug 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=10 Aug 2025}}</ref> New signings Zubimendi and Gyökeres combined for the opening goal, as the Swedish striker planted a header into the far side of the goal following a first-time cross from the Spaniard. Incisive football then saw [[Gabriel Martinelli]] put through on goal and set up Saka for a calm side foot finish into an unguarded net. [[Kai Havertz]] rounded off the scoring with a powerful run and an accomplished left foot strike, low and across the goalkeeper.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-ath-bilbao/report/537991 |title=Arsenal 3-0 Athletic Club: Viktor Gyokeres off the mark for Gunners who end pre-season with emphatic win |date=9 Aug 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=10 Aug 2025}}</ref> The subsequent penalty shootout saw Raya make one save and Arsenal score six of their seven penalties to win 6–5. The Player of the Match, Zubimendi, scored the decisive winning penalty.<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Arsenal F.C. |user=Arsenal |number=1954286815579443427 |date=9 Aug 2025 |title=The conductor &#x26A1; |access-date=10 Aug 2025}}</ref>

====First team transfers (summer transfer window)====
The Premier League [[List of English football transfers summer 2025|summer transfer window]] ran from 1 June to 10 June (due to an exceptional registration period mandated by [[FIFA]] for the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|Club World Cup]]), and then between 16 June and 1 September 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4272739 |title=Summer 2025 Transfer Window dates and times confirmed |date=14 May 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal confirmed on 4 June that they were to release twenty players,<ref name="Retained List">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/contract-updates-20-players-depart-summer |title=Contract updates: 20 players to depart this summer |date=4 Jun 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 Jun 2025}}</ref> two of whom, [[Kieran Tierney]] and [[Jorginho (footballer, born December 1991)|Jorginho]], had made 144 and 79 appearances for the Gunners' first team in all competitions respectively.

On 5 June, the club confirmed that Portuguese defender [[Nuno Tavares]], who had spent the entire previous season on loan with [[Serie A]] side [[SS Lazio|Lazio]], joined the Italian team on a permanent transfer,<ref name="Tavares departed AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/nuno-tavares-joins-lazio-on-permanent-deal-aHjyx0U6M1Qc |title=Nuno Tavares joins Lazio on permanent deal |date=5 Jun 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref> for a previously agreed fee reported to be [[Euro|€]]9&nbsp;million ([[Pound sterling|£]]7.6&nbsp;million).<ref name="Tavares fee">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5638415/2024/07/16/manchester-united-transfer-latest-real-madrid-arsenal/ |title=The Transfer DealSheet: Latest on Man Utd, Arsenal, Liverpool, Real Madrid, Barcelona and more |author=The Athletic Staff |author-link=The Athletic |date=16 Jul 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=5 Jun 2025}}</ref> It was then confirmed four days later that another loan had been made permanent as Brazilian forward [[Marquinhos (footballer, born 2003)|Marquinhos]], who had been on loan at [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] side [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] since January 2025, joined the Brazilian club in a permanent transfer for a reported fee of £3&nbsp;million.<ref name="Marquinhos departed AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/marquinhos-joins-cruzeiro |title=Marquinhos joins Cruzeiro |date=9 Jun 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=9 Jun 2025}}</ref><ref name="Marquinhos fee">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6413081/2025/06/10/arsenal-transfer-latest-news-manchester-united-liverpool-chelsea-barcelona-real-madrid/ |title=The Transfer DealSheet: Latest on Man Utd, Arsenal, Liverpool, Real Madrid and more |author=The Athletic Staff |date=10 Jun 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=10 Jun 2025}}</ref>

On 1 July, the club confirmed that they had completed their first signing of the summer (and under new Sporting Director [[Andrea Berta]]) as 30-year-old Spanish goalkeeper [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] joined from London [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|rivals]] [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on a long-term deal.<ref name="Kepa joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/kepa-arrizabalaga-signs-arsenal |title=Kepa Arrizabalaga signs for Arsenal |date=1 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Jul 2025}}</ref> The goalkeeper had spent the past two seasons on loan at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (where he won [[2023–24 La Liga|La Liga]], the [[2024 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]) and [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]]. Arsenal activated a £5&nbsp;million release clause in his Chelsea contract to complete the deal.<ref name="Kepa fee and contract"/> Kepa became the seventeenth Spaniard to play for the club and remained, at the time of his signing, the most expensive goalkeeper ever purchased, after his £72&nbsp;million move to Chelsea in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/keeping-kepa-13-facts-about-our-no-13 |title=Keeping up with Kepa: 13 facts about our No. 13 |last=Peat |first=Charlie |date=1 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=3 Jul 2025}}</ref>

On 4 July, the club confirmed that a mutual agreement had been reached to terminate the contract of Japanese international [[Takehiro Tomiyasu]] twelve months early after injuries had limited the defender's availability on the pitch in the past two seasons. Tomiyasu made 84 appearances at the club and was awarded the club's Player of the Month in both September 2021 and October 2023.<ref name="Tomiyasu departed AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/takehiro-tomiyasu-depart-arsenal |title=Takehiro Tomiyasu to depart Arsenal |date=4 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 Jul 2025}}</ref>

On 6 July, the club confirmed their second signing of the summer window as 26-year-old Spanish midfielder [[Martín Zubimendi]] joined from [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] side [[Real Sociedad]] on a long-term deal.<ref name="Zubimendi joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/martin-zubimendi-signs-arsenal |title=Martin Zubimendi signs for Arsenal |date=6 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=6 Jul 2025}}</ref> Arsenal agreed to pay €5&nbsp;million above the stipulated release clause in Zubimendi's contract to enable the transfer fee to be paid in multiple instalments, thus bringing the total figure up to €65&nbsp;million (£55.8&nbsp;million).<ref name="Zubimendi fee and contract"/> Zubimendi had connections to multiple club personnel at the time of joining, having been born in the same [[San Sebastián|city]] and played for the same [[Antiguoko|youth club]] as manager Mikel Arteta, whilst also having made appearances alongside Raya, Ødegaard and Merino (169 with the latter) at club and international level.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/get-know-zubimendi-these-12-fun-facts |title=Get to know Zubimendi with these 12 fun facts |last=Peat |first=Charlie |date=6 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=8 Jul 2025}}</ref>

Just four days later the club confirmed their third summer signing as 31-year-old Danish midfielder [[Christian Nørgaard]] joined from fellow [[Premier League]] and London club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on a long-term contract.<ref name="Norgaard joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/christian-norgaard-signs-arsenal |title=Christian Norgaard signs for Arsenal |date=10 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=10 Jul 2025}}</ref> The deal for the Bees' captain was concluded for an initial fee of £10&nbsp;million with potential performance related add-ons totalling £2&nbsp;million.<ref name="Norgaard fee and contract"/> As was the case for the two previous signings of the summer, Nørgaard joined forces with a former teammate, having played alongside Raya for four years at Brentford.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/get-know-norgaard-16-facts-our-new-signing |title=Get to know Norgaard: 16 facts on our new signing |last=Peat |first=Charlie |date=10 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=10 Jul 2025}}</ref>

The club's fourth signing, and second from Chelsea, of the summer window was confirmed on 18 July, as 23-year-old English forward [[Noni Madueke]] joined on a long-term contract.<ref name="Madueke joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/noni-madueke-signs-for-arsenal-avQGF3a6zcO1 |title=Noni Madueke signs for Arsenal |date=18 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=18 Jul 2025}}</ref> The Gunners agreed to pay an initial fee of £48.5&nbsp;million, rising to £52&nbsp;million with potential add-ons.<ref name="Madueke fee and contract"/> Whilst the signing was not initially deemed popular by sections of the fanbase,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c23gzevz398o |title=Why #NoToMadueke is trending among Arsenal fans |last=Howell |first=Alex |date=11 Jul 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=21 Jul 2025}}</ref> manager Mikel Arteta lauded the signing of "one of the most talented wide forward players in the Premier League".<ref name="Madueke joined AFC"/>

On 24 July, the club confirmed their fifth signing of the summer window as 21-year-old Spanish defender [[Cristhian Mosquera]] joined from [[La Liga]] side [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on a long-term deal.<ref name="Mosquera joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/cristhian-mosquera-signs-arsenal |title=Cristhian Mosquera signs for Arsenal |date=24 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 Jul 2025}}</ref> The deal was concluded for a total package reported to be under €20&nbsp;million, consisting of an initial fee of €15&nbsp;million (£13&nbsp;million).<ref name="Mosquera fee"/> Mosquera arrived in North London with experience beyond his years; since becoming the youngest centre back in Valencia's history at the time of his debut, he had gone on to be an almost ever-present feature of their defence for the past two seasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/cristhian-mosquera-story-so-far |title=Cristhian Mosquera: The story so far |last=Peat |first=Charlie |date=24 Jul 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 Jul 2025}}</ref>

Just two days later, Arsenal confirmed their sixth signing of the summer window at 27-year-old Swedish striker [[Viktor Gyökeres]] joined from [[Primeira Liga|Portuguese]] side [[Sporting CP|Sporting]] on a long-term deal.<ref name="Gyokeres joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/viktor-gyokeres-signs-arsenal |title=Viktor Gyökeres signs for Arsenal |date=26 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=26 Jul 2025}}</ref> After protracted negotiations, the deal was concluded for an initial fee of €63.5&nbsp;million (£55&nbsp;million) plus an additional €10&nbsp;million (£8.7&nbsp;million) in potential add-ons.<ref name="Gyokeres fee and contract"/> Over the course of his two years at Sporting, Gyökeres became one of the most prolific strikers in Europe, netting 97 times in 102 games, winning the Title and Golden Boot in [[List of Portuguese football champions#List of champions and top scorers|back-to-back seasons]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4358817/arsenal-sign-striker-gyokeres-from-sporting |title=Arsenal sign striker Gyokeres from Sporting |date=26 Jul 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=27 Jul 2025}}</ref> Such was the profile of his signing that demand for Gyokeres' number 14 shirt exceeded that of any signing in the club's history, breaking sales records and momentarily crashing the club's official website.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6522378/2025/07/29/viktor-gyokeres-arsenal-shirt-record/ |title=Viktor Gyokeres shirt sales break Arsenal record |last=McNicholas |first=James |date=29 Jul 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=29 Jul 2025}}</ref>

The club's outgoings (aside from contract expirations and terminations) began on 22 August, as [[Karl Hein (footballer)|Karl Hein]] departed for [[Bundesliga]] side [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] on a season-long loan.<ref name="Hein loaned out AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/karl-hein-joins-werder-bremen-loan |title=Karl Hein joins Werder Bremen on loan |date=22 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=22 Aug 2025}}</ref> It was the Estonian's third separate loan away from the club since joining in 2018.

As the transfer window neared its conclusion, Arsenal announced their seventh signing on 23 August, as former [[Arsenal F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Academy]] graduate [[Eberechi Eze]] re-joined the club following his release at the age of 13.<ref name="Eze joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/eberechi-eze-signs-arsenal |title=Eberechi Eze signs for Arsenal |date=23 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=23 Aug 2025}}</ref> Eze signed from fellow [[Football in London|London]] club [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on a long-term contract for an initial fee of £60&nbsp;million plus an additional £7.5&nbsp;million in potential add-ons (which, at that time, represented the club's third largest total-package purchase in their [[List of Arsenal F.C. records and statistics#Transfers|history]]).<ref name="Eze fee and contract"/> Having joined the club on the back of North London rivals [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] agreeing a deal for the player, whilst also echoing the move of club legend [[Ian Wright]] from South to North London, Eze was heavily revered by the fanbase during his unveiling to the [[Emirates Stadium|Emirates]] crowd prior to kick off in the first home game of the season against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c5y077p4z7vo |title='A creative and explosive talent' - Eze signs for Arsenal |last=Mallows |first=Tom |date=23 Aug 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=26 Aug 2025}}</ref>

In what proved to be a very busy [[Transfer deadline day|deadline day]], the club announced the departures of six players starting with [[Albert Sambi Lokonga]] joining German side [[Hamburger SV]] in a permanent deal, having spent much of his four years at the club away on loan.<ref name="Lokonga departed AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/sambi-lokonga-joins-hamburger-sv |title=Sambi Lokonga joins Hamburger SV |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref> [[Jakub Kiwior]] departed in a loan deal to Portuguese side [[FC Porto|Porto]] which included a €2&nbsp;million (£1.7&nbsp;million) loan fee, an obligation to make the move permanent for a total package worth €22&nbsp;million (£19&nbsp;million) inclusive of add-ons, plus a payment of €2&nbsp;million (£1.7&nbsp;million) if Kiwior secures a move away from Porto in the future.<ref name="Kiwior fee">{{cite web |url=https://www.fcporto.pt/pt/noticias/20250901-pt-comunicado-jakub-kiwior |title=Comunicado: Jakub Kiwior |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=FC Porto |access-date=1 Sep 2025 |language=pt |trans-title=Communication: Jakub Kiwior}}</ref> Kiwior made 68 appearances across two and a half years at the club and was a notable member of the defence that went to the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Semi-finals|UEFA Champions League Semi finals]] in the previous season.<ref name="Kiwior loaned out AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/jakub-kiwior-joins-porto-season-long-loan |title=Jakub Kiwior joins Porto on season-long loan |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref> Two long-standing members of the squad, having each made 90+ appearances for the club, then departed on loan as [[Oleksandr Zinchenko (footballer)|Oleksandr Zinchenko]]<ref name="Zinchenko loaned out AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/zinchenko-joins-nottingham-forest-loan |title=Zinchenko joins Nottingham Forest on loan |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref> and [[Reiss Nelson]] joined Premier League sides [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] respectively. Nelson had graduated from the club's academy and had been at the club for 17 years at the time of his departure.<ref name="Nelson loaned out AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/reiss-nelson-joins-brentford-loan-0 |title=Reiss Nelson joins Brentford on loan |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref> Lastly, [[Fábio Vieira (footballer, born 2000)|Fábio Vieira]] joined Lokonga as he made a loan move to Hamburger SV,<ref name="Vieira loaned out AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/fabio-vieira-joins-hamburger-sv-loan |title=Fabio Vieira joins Hamburger SV on loan |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref> with an option to make the move permanent,<ref name="Vieira fee">{{cite web |url=https://www.getfootballnewsgermany.com/2025/official-hamburg-conclude-bundesliga-transfer-coup-of-the-summer-with-fabio-vieira-signing/ |title=Official {{pipe}} Hamburg conclude 'Bundesliga transfer coup of the summer' with Fabio Vieira signing |last=Weis |first=Peter |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Get Germany Football News |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref> and Academy player Lucas Nygaard make the loan switch to [[Danish 2nd Division]] side [[Brabrand IF|Brabrand]].<ref name="Nygaard loaned out AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/lucas-martin-nygaard-joins-brabrand-if-loan |title=Lucas Martin Nygaard joins Brabrand IF on loan |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref>

Compensating for Kiwior's loan move to Porto, the club then announced their eighth and final signing of the summer window, as Ecuadorian defender [[Piero Hincapié]] joined in a season-long loan move from [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]].<ref name="Hincapie loaned in AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/piero-hincapie-completes-loan-move-arsenal |title=Piero Hincapie completes loan move to Arsenal |date=1 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=1 Sep 2025}}</ref> The deal included an option to make the move permanent for a total package of €52&nbsp;million (£45&nbsp;million).<ref name="Hincapie fee"/> Hincapié played a crucial part in Leverkusen's Invincible run to the [[2023–24 Bundesliga|League]] and [[2023–24 DFB-Pokal|Cup]] double in the [[2023–24 in German football|2023–24 season]], and upon his signing, became the first Ecuadorian in history to represent the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/piero-hincapie-his-story-so-far |title=Piero Hincapie: His story so far |last=Peat |first=Charlie |date=1 Sep 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 Sep 2025}}</ref>

===August===

{{football squad on pitch|align=right|flag_template=flagg2

| RB_nat = ENG | RB = White
| RCB_nat = FRA | RCB = Saliba
| LCB_nat = BRA | LCB = Gabriel

| RCM_nat = NOR | RCM = Ødegaard (c)
| DM_nat = ESP | DM = Zubimendi

| CF_nat = SWE | CF = Gyökeres 
| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3 formation]]) for Premier League away match against Manchester United on 17 August<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting Lineups - Man Utd vs Arsenal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/manchester-united-vs-arsenal/teams/531137 |website=Sky Sports |date=17 August 2025 |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>}}
Arsenal began the [[Premier League]] season with a 0–1 away win against rivals [[Manchester United]] at [[Old Trafford]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Marsh |first=Charlotte |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13412272/manchester-united-0-1-arsenal-riccardo-calafiori-header-sees-gunners-edge-to-premier-league-opening-weekend-win |title=Manchester United 0-1 Arsenal: Riccardo Calafiori header sees Gunners edge to Premier League opening-weekend win |website=Sky Sports |publisher=Sky Group |date=18 August 2025}}</ref> [[Riccardo Calafiori]] scored the match's only goal with a close-range header, converting [[Declan Rice]]'s inswinging corner after United goalkeeper [[Altay Bayindir]] failed to deal with it.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester United 0-1 Arsenal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Aug-17/manchester-united-0-1-arsenal-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=17 August 2025 |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref> This result extended Arsenal's unbeaten run against Manchester United in the Premier League to six games, the last defeat coming on 4 September 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask?q=arsenal+record+vs+united+from+1%2F22%2F2023+to+8%2F17%2F2025 |title=Arsenal record vs Manchester United from 1/22/2023 to 8/17/2025 |website=StatMuse |access-date=18 September 2025}}</ref>

On 23 August 2025, Arsenal secured their first home victory of the season, defeating newly promoted [[Leeds United]] 5–0 at the [[Emirates Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arsenal 5-0 Leeds United Match Report |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Aug-23/arsenal-5-0-leeds-united-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=23 August 2025 |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>
[[Jurrien Timber]] scored twice, both from corner situations, and also provided an assist for Saka, who finished with a strike from his weaker foot. In the second half, summer signing  Gyökeres scored his first goal for the club, making a brilliant solo run past multiple Leeds defenders before slotting home a through ball from Calafiori into the near bottom corner. The game saw [[Max Dowman]] make his Premier League debut, coming on as a substitute for Arsenal in the 64th minute of their match, becoming the second youngest player in the league's history at 15 years and 235 days, behind only teammate Nwaneri.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 August 2025 |title=Gyokeres hits double as Arsenal put FIVE past Leeds |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4387431/gyokeres-hits-double-as-arsenal-put-five-past-leeds |access-date=23 August 2025 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref> He won a penalty for his team in the third minute of stoppage time, with Gyokeres converting it for his brace.<ref>{{cite web |last=Howell |first=Alex |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/crm4p9xkwlko |title=Arsenal's Dowman, 15, shines on Premier League debut |website=BBC Sport |date=23 August 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal suffered their first defeat of the season, losing 0–1 to [[Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]] on 31 August.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Aug-31/liverpool-1-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Liverpool 1-0 Arsenal: Match report |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=31 August 2025}}</ref> With an injury-hit squad, Mikel Arteta started Merino and Madueke as replacements for the unavailable Ødegaard and Saka.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Team news: Two changes made for Liverpool test |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-two-changes-made-liverpool-test |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=31 August 2025 |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>
Arsenal suffered an early setback four minutes into the match, with Saliba leaving the field due to injury and being replaced by summer signing Mosquera.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=Nick |title=Cristian Mosquera eases William Saliba dependence as Arsenal's £13m bargain buy impresses |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13433802/cristian-mosquera-eases-william-saliba-dependence-as-arsenals-13m-bargain-buy-impresses-the-radar |website=Sky Sports |date=21 September 2025 |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref> Both sides struggled to create chances until [[Dominik Szoboszlai]] scored a 30-yard free-kick in the final ten minutes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Gregg |last2=de Roché |first2=Art |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6587211/2025/08/31/liverpool-arsenal-premier-league-szoboszlai/ |title=Liverpool 1 Arsenal 0: Incredible Szoboszlai free kick from distance wins it at Anfield |website=The Athletic via The New York Times |date=31 August 2025}}</ref> The result ended Arsenal's 22-game unbeaten streak against Top Six opposition, a run that had begun on 2 May 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask?q=arsenal+all-time+record+against+the+big+six+from+5%2F2%2F2023+to+8%2F31%2F2025 |title=Arsenal all-time record against the Big Six from 5/2/2023 to 8/31/2025 |website=StatMuse |access-date=18 September 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal had an injury-hit August, with Havertz, Saka, Ødegaard, and Saliba all sustaining injuries during these matches, sidelining them for weeks or, in some cases, months.<ref>{{cite web |last=Keith |first=Felix |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsenal-transfers-injuries-gyokeres-mosquera-35924728 |title=Arsenal's summer transfer window seen in new light as early injury crisis strikes |website=mirror.co.uk |publisher=Mirror |date=18 September 2025}}</ref>

===September===

Fifteen Arsenal players, excluding those out on loan, were called up to their national senior squads for [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international fixtures]] in September: Rice, Madueke, Lewis-Skelly and Eze (England); Raya, Zubimendi and Merino (Spain); Gabriel Magalhães and Martinelli (Brazil); Gyökeres (Sweden); Trossard (Belgium); Calafiori (Italy); Timber (Netherlands); Ødegaard (Norway, captain); and Hincapié (Ecuador).<ref>{{cite web |title=Internationals: World Cup qualifiers — 16 stars |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/internationals-world-cup-qualifiers-16-stars |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3 formation]]) for Champions League away match against Athletic Bilbao on 16 September<ref>{{Cite web |title=Athletic Club vs Arsenal: Line-ups |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2045908--athletic-club-vs-arsenal/lineups/ |website=UEFA.com |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>}}
On 13 September, returning from the international break, Arsenal secured their third league win with a 3–0 victory over [[Nottingham Forest]], with Zubimendi scoring his first brace in top-flight football, Gyökeres netting his third goal in four league games, and Raya making his 100th appearance for the club.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal 3–0 Nottingham Forest |date=13 September 2025 |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Sep-13/arsenal-3-0-nottingham-forest-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref> On 16 September 2025, Arsenal began their [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] campaign with a 0–2 away win against [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Bate |first=Adam |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11945/13431632/athletic-club-0-2-arsenal-substitutes-gabriel-martinelli-and-leandro-trossard-secure-champions-league-win-in-bilbao |title=Athletic Club 0-2 Arsenal: Substitutes Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard secure Champions League win in Bilbao |website=Sky Sports |publisher=Sky Group |date=16 September 2025}}</ref>

On 21 September, Arsenal played [[Manchester City]] in the Premier League at the Emirates Stadium.<ref>{{cite web |title=Preview: Arsenal v Manchester City |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-manchester-city-1 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref> [[Erling Haaland]] gave City an early lead from a counter-attack, but Arsenal equalised late on when substitute Martinelli lobbed [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]] after a pass from Eze.<ref>{{cite web |title=Martinelli's LATE equaliser rescues point for Arsenal against Man City |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4413692/arsmci-report |website=PremierLeague.com |date=21 September 2025 |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref> The match ended 1–1, with [[Mikel Arteta]] becoming the first manager to avoid defeat in five consecutive league games against [[Pep Guardiola]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal 1-1 Manchester City |date=21 September 2025 |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Sep-21/arsenal-1-1-manchester-city-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal began their [[2025–26 EFL Cup]] campaign in the third round with a 0–2 away win against League One side [[Port Vale]] on 24 September.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sky Sports |title=Port Vale 0-2 Arsenal: Eberechi Eze scores first goal for Gunners as they progress in Carabao Cup third-round tie |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13436557/port-vale-0-2-arsenal-eberechi-eze-scores-first-goal-for-gunners-as-they-progress-in-carabao-cup-third-round-tie |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref> The match marked Kepa's competitive debut for the club, with Eze also scoring his first goal for Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Port Vale 0-2 Arsenal |date=24 September 2025 |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Sep-24/port-vale-0-2-arsenal-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>

On 29 September, Arsenal secured a 1–2 away win against [[Newcastle United]] in the Premier League, moving into second place and closing the gap to leaders Liverpool to two points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Newcastle 1–2 Arsenal |date=28 September 2025 |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Sep-28/newcastle-united-1-2-arsenal-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=28 September 2025}}</ref> Newcastle opened the scoring in the 34th minute when [[Nick Woltemade]] headed in a cross from Sandro Tonali past Raya, with Gabriel Magalhães partially at fault for failing to challenge effectively.<ref name="Waugh">{{Cite news |last=Waugh |first=Chris |title=Newcastle 1 Arsenal 2: Gabriel's redemption? Livramento blow? Calafiori towel incident? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6670447/2025/09/28/newcastle-arsenal-result-report-analysis/ |work=The New York Times |date=28 September 2025 |access-date=28 September 2025}}</ref> In the 84th minute, Merino headed in a cross from Rice to level the scores, before Gabriel Magalhães scored a stoppage-time header from a corner to secure a win for Arsenal, redeeming himself for his earlier involvement in Newcastle's opener.<ref name="Waugh"/> With the win, Arsenal put an end to their three-game losing streak at [[St James' Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Louise |title=Gabriel Magalhães stuns Newcastle with last-gasp comeback winner for Arsenal |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/sep/28/newcastle-arsenal-premier-league-match-report |website=The Guardian |date=28 September 2025 |access-date=28 September 2025}}</ref>

===October===

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1 formation]]) for Premier League away match against Fulham on 18 October<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting Lineups - Fulham vs Arsenal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/fulham-vs-arsenal/teams/531202|website=Sky Sports |date=18 October 2025 |access-date=16 January 2026}}</ref>}}
Arsenal began the month with a 2–0 home win against [[Olympiacos]] in the Champions League on 1 October.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Live: Arsenal vs Olympiacos |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn95znpj2pgt |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> Martinelli opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a tap-in after Gyökeres's effort struck the post, before Saka sealed the victory in second-half stoppage time with a low finish between the legs of Olympiacos goalkeeper [[Konstantinos Tzolakis]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arsenal 2-0 Olympiacos – Match Report |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Oct-01/arsenal-2-0-olympiacos-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=1 October 2025 |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref>

On 4 October, the Gunners welcomed fellow London side [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] to the Emirates. Rice opened the scoring in the 38th minute against his former club, following a saved Eze shot. In the 66th minute, Arsenal were awarded a penalty as ''Hammers'' defender [[El Hadji Malick Diouf|Malick Diouf]] hauled Timber down in the box. Saka successfully converted, giving the Gunners a comfortable two goal cushion with half an hour to play. West Ham could not find a breakthrough throughout the remainder of the match, as Arsenal became the league leaders with 18 points heading into the second international break of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-0 West Ham United|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Oct-04/arsenal-2-0-west-ham-united-match-report |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=30 October 2025|date=4 October 2025|last=Rogers|first=Jonathon}}</ref>

Fifteen Arsenal players (excluding players who were loaned out) were named in their respective countries' senior squads for international fixtures in October: Rice, Saka, Lewis-Skelly and Eze (England); Raya, Zubimendi and Merino (Spain); Gabriel Magalhães and Martinelli (Brazil); Gyökeres (Sweden); Trossard (Belgium); Calafiori (Italy); Timber (Netherlands); Saliba (France); and Nørgaard (Denmark).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Where and when our internationals are in action|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/international-preview-15-stars-october-action|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=30 October 2025|date=7 October 2025|last=Peat|first=Charlie}}</ref>

With the conclusion of the international break, Arsenal traveled to [[Craven Cottage]] on 18 October to face [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] in the league. A goal from [[Leandro Trossard]] in the second half gave the Gunners a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Fulham 0-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Oct-18/fulham-0-1-arsenal-match-report|access-date=30 October 2025|date=18 October 2025|last=James|first=Josh|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref> On 21 October, Arsenal returned to the Emirates to host Spanish [[La Liga]] giants [[Atlético Madrid]] in the Champions League. Goals from Gabriel, Martinelli, and a brace from Gyökeres handed the Gunners a 4–0 win over the visitors. This triumph meant Arsenal had amassed 9 points from a possible 9 in the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League league phase|league phase]], placing them fourth in the league standings.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 4-0 Atletico Madrid|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Oct-21/arsenal-4-0-atletico-madrid-match-report|access-date=30 October 2025|date=21 October 2025|last=Rogers|first=Jonathon|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 26 October, Arsenal played Crystal Palace at the Emirates for their second [[London derbies|London Derby]] in eight days. In a relatively tame match, Eze netted the only goal, against his former club. The result meant the Gunners were now four points clear of second position [[A.F.C. Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] in the league, coming after slip-ups from Manchester City and title-defenders Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 1-0 Crystal Palace|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Oct-26/arsenal-1-0-crystal-palace-match-report|access-date=30 October 2025|date=26 October 2025|last=Rogers|first=Jonathon|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arsenal followed their success against Palace with a 2–0 home defeat of [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]] in the Carabao Cup, with goals from Nwaneri and Saka sending them into the Quarter-Finals of the tournament. Arteta rotated the squad heavily, handing out first competitive starts to Hale End products Dowman and [[Andre Harriman-Annous]], along with new signing Hincapié. The Gunners were later drawn to Crystal Palace for the Quarter-Finals of the cup, whom they had beaten three days prior.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-0 Brighton|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Oct-29/arsenal-2-0-brighton-hove-albion-match-report|access-date=30 October 2025|date=29 October 2025|last=Peat|first=Charlie|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

===November===

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1 formation]]) for Champions League home match against Bayern Munich on 26 November<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting Lineups - Bayern Munich vs Arsenal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-bayern-munich/teams/547992|website=Sky Sports |date=26 November 2025 |access-date=16 January 2026}}</ref>}}
The Gunners started the month with a 0–2 away win against newly promoted side [[Burnley F.C|Burnley]] on 1 November, with two headers in the first half from Gyökeres and Rice. Trossard made his 100th appearance in the league for Arsenal, having already done so at [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Burnley 0-2 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Nov-01/burnley-0-2-arsenal-match-report|date=1 November 2025|access-date=7 November 2025|last=Peat|first=Charlie|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 4 November, Arteta's men made the trip to [[Czech Republic|Czechia]] for their Champions League fixture against  [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]]. The Gunners proved to be too strong for the [[Czech First League]] champions, and courtesy of a Merino brace and Saka penalty, came away with a 3–0 victory, shooting them up to 2nd place in the league standings. This success marked the first time Arsenal had kept eight clean sheets in a row in all competitions since 1903, and the first time Arteta had won ten in a row in his managerial career. Hale End products Dowman and Harriman-Annous came on in the second half, with the former becoming the youngest Champions League player in history at 15 years and 308 days old.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Slavia Prague 0-3 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-slavia-prague-0-3-arsenal|date=4 November 2025|access-date=7 November 2025|last=James|first=Josh|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Following their triumph in Prague, Arsenal traveled to the [[Stadium of Light]] for their league match against 4th-placed [[Sunderland]]. Their newly promoted opponents were captained by former Gunner [[Granit Xhaka]], whom had departed the North London side two years prior for Bayer Leverkusen. The hosts gained a 1–0 lead heading into the interval, with a [[Dan Ballard (footballer)|Dan Ballard]] finish past Raya in the 36th minute. In the second half, the Gunners returned to the pitch with a renewed energy, finding the back of the net twice in twenty minutes owing to strikes from Saka and Trossard. However, despite having seemingly completing the turnaround, the visitors were unable to hold on to their advantage as Sunderland substitute [[Brian Brobbey]] equalised in stoppage time with an overhead kick. The 2–2 draw ended Arsenal's winning run and reduced their lead on 2nd-placed Manchester City to four points, heading into the third and final international break of the year.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Sunderland 2-2 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Nov-08/sunderland-2-2-arsenal-match-report|date=8 November 2025|access-date=13 November 2025|last=Rogers|first=Jonathon|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Thirteen Arsenal players (excluding players who were loaned out) joined up with their respective countries' senior squads for international fixtures in October: Rice, Saka, and Eze (England); Raya, Zubimendi and Merino (Spain); Gabriel Magalhães (Brazil); Trossard (Belgium); Calafiori (Italy); Timber (Netherlands); Saliba (France); Nørgaard (Denmark); and Hincapié (Ecuador).<ref>{{Cite web|title=13 Gunners picked for November internationals|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/13-gunners-picked-november-internationals|date=13 November 2025|access-date=13 November 2025|last=Peat|first=Charlie|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 23 November, the Gunners continued their Premier League campaign with a [[North London derby]] at home against Tottenham Hotspur. With Gabriel Magalhães out injured, Arteta handed summer recruit Hincapié his first league start. In the 36th minute, Trossard gave the hosts a 1–0 advantage with a turn and shot inside the box. This was followed by a second goal from a right-footed Eze shot shortly before the interval. At the start of the second half, Eze doubled up to make it three for the Gunners, finishing into the bottom-corner of Tottenham goalkeeper [[Guglielmo Vicario]]'s net. In the 54th minute, opposing striker [[Richarlison]] beat Raya from long range to reduce the deficit to two, but Arsenal's three-goal advantage was restored as Eze netted his third of the night, rounding off his first career hat-trick and a 4–1 pounding of the visitors.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 4-1 Tottenham Hotspur|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Nov-23/arsenal-4-1-tottenham-hotspur-match-report|date=23 November 2025|access-date=29 November 2025|last=James|first=Josh|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arsenal hosted reigning Bundesliga champions [[Bayern Munich]] in a blockbuster Champions League league phase fixture on 26 November. Both sides were even on twelve points in the league standings heading into the match, with four wins apiece. Arteta made two adjustments to the squad that had defeated Tottenham Hotspur three days prior, replacing Hincapié with Mosquera at centre-back, and Calafiori with Lewis-Skelly at left-back. After a period of relatively cagey opening exchanges, the Gunners took the lead as Timber nodded in Saka's corner from close range. However, succeeding a wasted Eze opportunity to double the lead, Bayern youngster [[Lennart Karl]] equalised at the other end to level the score 1–1. Following the break, Arsenal began churning out chances, with Saka, Merino, Mosquera, and Rice all squandering attempts to retake the advantage. Finally, in the 69th minute, subtitutes Calafiori and Madueke combined to provide the breakthrough for the Gunners, with the former assisting the latter's first goal for the club. Another of Arteta's changes, Martinelli, also made an impact, as he made a run to receive Eze's lofted pass, before beating Bayern goalkeeper [[Manuel Neuer]] near the halfway line and finishing into an empty net to complete the 3–1 victory. This success placed Arsenal top of the league phase standings, and dealt Bayern's first defeat of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 3-1 Bayern MunichHotspur|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Nov-26/arsenal-3-1-bayern-munich-match-report|access-date=29 November 2025|last=James|first=Josh|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=26 November 2025}}</ref>

On 30 November, the Gunners crossed the capital to face 3rd-placed Chelsea away at the [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]]. After a goalless first half that saw Chelsea midfielder [[Moisés Caicedo]] sent off for a challenge on Merino, [[Trevor Chalobah]] gave the hosts the lead with a header past Raya in the 48th minute. The visitors responded eleven minutes later, with Merino nodding in a Saka cross for the equaliser. Arteta's side were unable to find a winner for the remainder of the half and were forced to settle with a 1–1 stalemate, with 2nd position Manchester City shortening the gap between them to five points.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Match report: Chelsea 1-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Nov-30/chelsea-1-1-arsenal-match-report|access-date=30 November 2025|last=James|first=Josh|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=30 November 2025}}</ref>

===December===

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3 formation]]) for Premier League home match against Wolves on 13 December<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting Lineups - Arsenal vs Wolverhampton Wanderers |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-wolverhampton-wanderers/teams/531279|website=Sky Sports |date=13 December 2025 |access-date=16 January 2026}}</ref>}}
The Gunners began the month with a home match against [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on 3 December. White and Ødegaard were named in the starting XI together for the first time since 17 August, when both started the opening fixture of the campaign against Manchester United. Merino gave the hosts an early lead, heading in a cross from White in the 11th minute. In second-half stoppage time, substitute Saka sealed the victory with a shot off Brentford goalkeeper [[Caoimhín Kelleher]]. The 2–0 result was Arsenal's fourth consecutive league win at the Emirates, their longest run of successive home league wins since a string of 5 triumphs in April 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-0 Brentford|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-03/arsenal-2-0-brentford-match-report|date=3 December 2025|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=6 December 2025}}</ref>

On 6 December, Arsenal traveled to [[Villa Park]] to face 3rd position [[Aston Villa F.C|Aston Villa]] in the league. In the 36th minute, [[Matty Cash]] broke the deadlock in favor of Villa, striking between the legs of Raya. Arteta made two changes during the break, with Trossard and Gyökeres replacing Eze and Merino. The former made an immediate impact, finishing a Saka cross to equalise on 52 minutes. However, Arteta's men were unable to find a crucial second goal, and [[Emiliano Buendía]] scored the winner for the hosts in the 4th minute of injury time. The defeat ended the visitors' 18-match unbeaten run in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Aston Villa 2-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-06/aston-villa-2-1-arsenal-match-report|date=6 December 2025|access-date=6 December 2025|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

The Gunners returned to the Champions League on 10 December, away to [[Club Brugge]]. In the 24th minute, Madueke recovered possession just inside the Brugge half, and netted a spectacular goal into the top-right corner from 25 yards out. Late on in the first half, Raya made several crucial saves to deny the hosts an equaliser. Arteta's side had the dream start after the interval, with Zubimendi finding an unmarked Madueke to score a second for the visitors. Martinelli followed suit in the 55th minute, curling in a stunner from outside the box. This goal made the Brazilian the first ever Arsenal player to score goals in five consecutive Champions League appearances. [[Gabriel Jesus]] came on just after the hour, making his competitive return after 332 days out with an [[anterior cruciate ligament injury]]. At 16 years and 103 days, [[Marli Salmon]] became the second-youngest Englishman in Champions League history, making his debut in the closing stages of the second half. The match ended 3–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Club Brugge 0-3 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-10/club-brugge-0-3-arsenal-match-report|date=10 December 2025|access-date=13 December 2025|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 13 December, the Gunners welcomed [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolves]] to the Emirates in a top-against-bottom league matchup. The visitors were able to frustrate Arteta's men, whom were unable to find the back of the net in the first half. The breakthrough finally came in the 70th minute, with a Saka corner ricocheting off the post, onto the back of Wolves goalkeeper [[Sam Johnstone]], and into the goal. Wolves began to pressure the hosts after the opener, culminating in a 90th minute headed finish from [[Tolu Arokodare]]. The away side's jubilation would be short lived, however, as Saka forced in an own goal once again, this time his delivery striking opposing defender [[Yerson Mosquera]] and finding the target. The 2–1 victory meant that Arsenal retained their 2-point gap at the top of the league summit.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-1 Wolves|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-13/arsenal-2-1-wolves-match-report|date=13 December 2025|access-date=15 December 2025|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arteta's men followed this success with a trip to [[Hill Dickinson Stadium]], the new home of 10th-placed [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]. A handball from opposing defender [[Jake O'Brien (footballer)|Jake O'Brien]] inside the box handed Arsenal a 27th-minute penalty, which was powerfully dispatched by Gyökeres. In the second half, Trossard was fed a through pass by Rice and unleashed a potent shot onto the post. The visitors missed many key chances to double their lead, but saw out a crucial triumph to remain ahead of 2nd position Manchester City.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Everton 0-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-20/everton-0-1-arsenal-match-report|date=20 December 2025|access-date=5 January 2026|first=Arsenal|last=Media|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 23 December, the Gunners returned to the Emirates to face Crystal Palace in the quarter-final round of the Carabao Cup. Arteta posted a rotated lineup, opting for a frontline of Martinelli, Jesus, and Madueke. Arsenal gradually built up pressure following the opening stages of the match, with Martinelli, Calafiori, Jesus, Timber, and Madueke all exchanging chances. Palace keeper [[Walter Benítez (footballer)|Walter Benítez]] made several key saves to deny the hosts the advantage. The South London visitors emerged a different side after the break, as opposing manager [[Oliver Glasner]] chose to bring on [[Justin Devenny]] and [[Nathaniel Clyne]] in place of first-half strugglers [[Edward Nketiah]] and [[Jaydee Canvot]]. These changes certainly helped the ''Eagles'', whom were able to prevent any Arsenal breakthrough for a greater period of the second half. In the 80th minute, the Gunners would finally break this resistance, forcing an own goal from a corner through opposing defender [[Maxence Lacroix]]. However, deep into stoppage time, Palace captain [[Marc Guehi]] was able to equalise with a close-range finish, forcing a penalty shootout. The ensuring shootout was of high quality, with both teams' first seven spot-kicks finding the back of the net. Saliba successfully beat Benitez for Arsenal's eighth, but Lacroix's attempt was palmed away by Arrizabalaga, sending Arteta's men to a second consecutive Carabao Cup semi-final, where they would play London [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 1-1 Crystal Palace (8-7 on pens)|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-23/arsenal-1-1-crystal-palace-match-report|date=23 December 2025|access-date=6 January 2026|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arsenal returned to league action with a 2–1 home win over Brighton & Hove Albion on 27 December. A first-half strike from Ødegaard and an own goal by [[Georginio Rutter]] gave Arteta's side a comfortable two-goal advantage before the hour mark, but the visitors rebounded, scoring through Paraguayan [[Diego Gómez (Paraguayan footballer)|Diego Gómez]] in the 64th minute. The ''Seagulls'' unsuccessfully pushed for an equaliser, with [[Yankuba Minteh]]'s curling shot saved by Raya and [[Mats Wieffer]]'s header missing the target. The Gunners were able to see another win out, securing a pivotal three points in the title race.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-1 Brighton & Hove Albion|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-27/arsenal-2-1-brighton-hove-albion-match-report|date=27 December 2025|access-date=10 January 2026|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

The Gunners finished 2025 with their second match of the month against 3rd position Aston Villa. [[Ollie Watkins]] missed several golden opportunities to put the visiting side ahead, leaving the scoreline level at 0–0 heading into the break. On 48 minutes, Gabriel found the opener, pouncing on an error from former teammate [[Emiliano Martínez]] to nod home a Saka corner. At 52 minutes, Zubimendi was sent through by Ødegaard, tucking a slick outside-the-boot finish past Martínez to find a second for the hosts. Trossard then turned the two goal advantage into three, unleashing from 20 yards to find the bottom-right corner. Substitute Jesus added a fourth goal, his first since 1 January, latching onto a Trossard ball in the 78th minute before turning it into the net. In stoppage time, Watkins netted a consolation from close range, as Villa's winning run was put to an end by a rampant Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 4-1 Aston Villa|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-30/arsenal-4-1-aston-villa-match-report|date=30 December 2025|access-date=11 January 2026|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

===January===

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3 formation]]) for Premier League home match against Manchester United on 25 January<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting Lineups - Arsenal vs Manchester United |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-manchester-united/teams/531349|website=Sky Sports |date=25 December 2025 |access-date=25 January 2026}}</ref>}}
Arsenal began 2026 with a trip to the South Coast to face [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] on 3 January. Wingers Saka and Trossard were rotated out in favor of Madueke and Martinelli, who were entrused to service Gyökeres in the center. On 10 minutes, a lapse in concentration from Gabriel saw the Brazilian centre-half play a square pass straight to [[Evanilson (footballer, born 1999)|Evanilson]], who calmly dispatched it past an out-of-position Raya. The Gunners would not be trailing for long, however, as a ricocheted Martinelli shot from a Madueke cross fell kindly to Gabriel, who redeemed himself with a first-time volley into the left side of the net. In the 54th minute, Ødegaard laid off Rice near the edge of the box, who scored to give the visitors the lead. Substitute Saka was then fed by Ødegaard, with the former cutting the ball back to Rice to score a third and his second of the night. The hosts responded with a stunner from [[Eli Junior Kroupi]], which set up a tense ending in which Arteta's side pulled through to secure another critical three points in the league.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Bournemouth 2-3 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-03/bournemouth-2-3-arsenal-match-report|date=3 January 2026|access-date=16 January 2026|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 8 January, the Gunners played reigning champions Liverpool at home. The hosts had the better of the first half, but were short of a cutting edge and failed to score. Arsenal were unable to carry the same momentum into the second period with Liverpool grew into control. The match ended goalless.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 0-0 Liverpool|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-08/arsenal-0-0-liverpool-match-report|date=8 January 2026|access-date=24 January 2026|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 11 January, Arsenal began their [[2025–26 FA Cup]] campaign in the third round, facing [[EFL Championship]] side [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] away. [[Colby Bishop]] gave the home side a shock lead early on with a close-range finish past Arrizabalaga, but Arsenal were quick to respond, forcing an own goal by [[Andre Dozzell]]. The visitors gradually swept aside Pompey through a Martinelli hattrick, despite a Madueke missed penalty. The 1–4 result propelled Arsenal to the fourth round of the competition, where they would be drawn to [[EFL League One]] side [[Wigan Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Portsmouth 1-4 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-11/portsmouth-1-4-arsenal-match-report|date=11 January 2026|access-date=24 January 2026|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arteta's men crossed the capital to face [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Chelsea for the [[2025–26 EFL Cup#Semi-Finals|EFL Cup semi-final]] first leg on 14 January. White's header gave the Gunners an early advantage, an advantage doubled by Gyökeres's tap-in on 49 minutes. [[Alejandro Garnacho]] pulled one back for the home side shortly after, striking between the legs of Arrizabalaga. Zubimendi restored the two-goal cushion with a composed finish in the 71st minute, before Garnacho struck again to end the tie 2–3 in favor of the visitors heading into the second leg on 3 February.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Chelsea 2-3 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-14/chelsea-2-3-arsenal-match-report|date=14 January 2026|access-date=24 January 2026|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Three days later, Arsenal faced Nottingham Forest away at the [[City Ground]] in the league. Neither side could find a breakthrough heading into the interval, with Martinelli shooting beyond the far post in what was the best chance of the half. In the 65th minute, [[Matz Sels]] denied Saka in a superb save to keep the tie level, before the Gunners had a penalty chalked off after a [[Ola Aina]] handball. The result condemned Arteta's side to consecutive 0–0 draws in the league, a first since the [[2012–13 Arsenal F.C. season|2012–13 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Nottingham Forest 0-0 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-17/nottingham-forest-0-0-arsenal-match-report|date=17 January 2026|access-date=24 January 2026|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arsenal played their fourth away game in ten days with a trip to [[San Siro]] to face Italian [[Serie A]] giants [[Inter Milan]] in the Champions League, a rematch of the [[2024–25 Arsenal F.C. season|previous season]]'s meeting between the two sides. Arteta made seven changes to the starting lineup from December's clash with Club Brugge, notably handing Jesus his first Champions League start of the season. The decision paid off quickly, as the Brazilian centre-forward nodded in a scuffed Timber shot in the 10th minute past [[Yann Sommer]] in the Inter goal. However, the preceding season's finalists would not be brushed aside so easily, with [[Petar Sucic]] finding the top-right corner on 18 minutes to equalise. The Gunners quickly responded to this setback, as an unmarked Trossard headed in dangerously from a Saka corner for Jesus to net his second of the night. Both teams exchanged numerous chances but neither side could find the back of the net for the remainer of the half. The game looked to be headed towards a nervy ending until Gyökeres sealed the victory with a long-ranged attempt in the 84th minute, sending the visitors through automatic qualification to the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|Round of 16]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Inter Milan 1-3 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-20/inter-milan-1-3-arsenal-match-report|date=20 January 2026|access-date=24 January 2026|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 25 January, Arsenal hosted 6th position Manchester United in the league, the reverse of the fixture between the two sides on Matchweek 1. Having made his first Champions League XI of the season in midweek, Jesus was entrusted to start his first Premier League match in 386 days. The Gunners dominated the early proceedings, with Zubimendi's header drawing a fine save by [[Senne Lammens]]. A [[Lisandro Martínez]] own goal just before the half hour gave the home side a deserved advantage, although it was quickly canceled out through a [[Bryan Mbeumo]] finish following a Zubimendi giveaway. On 50th minutes, United had the lead as [[Patrick Dorgu]]'s volley struck the woodwork and beat Raya, surviving a VAR check after. This forced a rare quadruple substitution from Arteta, who brought on White, Eze, Merino and Gyökeres in place of Hincapié, Ødegaard, Zubimendi, and Jesus. Merino repaid his manager in kind, netting a scrappy equaliser from point-blank range in the 84th minute. The hosts would only be briefly level, however, as [[Matheus Cunha]] dispatched an inch-perfect strike from outside the penalty area. The 2–3 defeat meant Arsenal were winless in three consecutive league games, had suffered their first competitive home loss of the campaign, and had conceded three goals in a match for the first time since a 4–3 win away at [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] during the [[2023–24 Arsenal F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-3 Manchester United|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-25/arsenal-2-3-manchester-united-match-report|date=25 January 2026|access-date=25 January 2026|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 28 January, the Gunners played host to Kazakh club [[FC Kairat]] in the final matchweek of the Champions League league phase. With a Round of 16 spot already secured and a pivotal league match against Leeds United upcoming, Arteta opted to rotate the starting lineup. On 3 minutes, Gyökeres splashed the ball into the bottom-corner to put the home side in front, assisted by injury-returnee Kai Havertz. Kairat answered just four minutes later, with Calafiori's shirt pull on [[Jorginho (footballer, born 1997)|Jorginho]] inside the penalty area setting up the Portuguese striker's equaliser from the spot. Havertz then contributed again, cracking a left-footed shot past [[Temirlan Anarbekov]] in the away goal. Martinelli added a third with a close-ranged finish in the 36th minute. Late into the second half, Arteta handed academy product [[Brando Bailey-Joseph]] a competitive debut, substituting the 17-year-old on in place of goalscorer Gyökeres. Kairat netted a consolation in stoppage time through [[Ricardinho (footballer, born 2001)|Ricardinho]], as Arsenal completed a flawless Champions League league phase, topping the 36-team table with 8 wins out of 8 matches.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 3-2 Kairat Almaty|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-28/arsenal-3-2-kairat-match-report|date=28 January 2026|access-date=31 January 2026|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arsenal closed January with a 0–4 success away at Leeds United, their fifth away win in all competitions in the month. Goals from Zubimendi, Madueke, Gyökeres and Jesus ended the visitors' 3-match winless streak, while restoring their 7-point lead at the top of the Premier League table.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Leeds United 0-4 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-31/leeds-united-0-4-arsenal-match-report|date=31 January 2026|access-date=31 January 2026|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

===February===
{{football squad on pitch|align=right|flag_template=flagg2

| DM_nat = ESP | DM = Zubimendi
