| CF_nat = SWE | CF = Gyökeres 
| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3 formation]]) for Premier League away match against Tottenham Hotspur on 22 February<ref>{{Cite web|title=Starting Lineups - Arsenal vs Spurs |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-hotspur-vs-arsenal/teams/531397|website=Sky Sports|date=22 February 2026 |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref>}}
Arsenal returned to the Emirates to face Chelsea for the second leg of their EFL Cup semi-final tie on 3 February. A goalless first half saw Hincapié's top-corner shot palmed away by [[Robert Sánchez]] before an [[Enzo Fernandez]] attempt was dealt with through Arizzabalaga. Already leading 3–2 on aggregate, Arteta's men defended resolutely in the second period to quell any fightback from the ''Blues''. Former Chelsea man Havertz was then brought on, finishing a superb Rice cross deep into stoppage time to send the home support into jubilation, and his team to the [[2026 EFL Cup final|competition final]] at [[Wembley Stadium]] on 22 March.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 1-0 Chelsea (4-2 agg)|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Feb-03/arsenal-1-0-chelsea-match-report|date=3 February 2026|access-date=8 February 2026|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 7 February, Arsenal welcomed 8th-placed Sunderland to the Emirates for a pivotal match in the league title race. Havertz came close to opening the scores within thirty seconds with an off-target header, and was then involved at the other end with a potential goal-preventing block on Sunderland forward Brian Brobbey's shot. Zubimendi gave the hosts a much-needed breakthrough on 42 minutes, striking perfectly beyond opposing goalkeeper [[Robin Roefs]] at the near post. Although trailing and without the momentum heading into the second half, it was [[Régis Le Bris]]'s ''Black Cats'' who emerged the brighter side following the break. [[Chemsdine Talbi]]'s effort was turned away by Raya, while Gabriel was forced into a sliding challenge on [[Trai Hume]] shortly after. The Gunners were able to reassert their dominance, though, as Gyökeres was put on with half an hour remaining and quickly scored to advance the game beyond the visitors' reach. The Swedish striker then netted again in injury time, opening Arsenal's advantage at the top of the table to nine points, ahead of Manchester City's clash with Liverpool.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 3-0 Sunderland|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Feb-07/arsenal-3-0-sunderland-match-report|date=7 February 2026|access-date=8 February 2026|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

The Gunners continued the month with a trip to the [[Gtech Community Stadium]] to play Brentford on 12 February. Following an unsatisfactory first half performance which saw Raya make a stunning stop on [[Igor Thiago]]'s header, the visitors came out of the interval with increased urgency. Madueke soon found an opener, heading against [[Caoimhín Kelleher]]'s momentum in the Brentford goal. The hosts were level just 10 minutes later, with [[Keane Lewis-Potter]] finding the back of the net from a [[Michael Kayode]] long throw-in. Neither team found a cutting edge in the remainder of the match, as Arteta's side had their nine-point lead at the top of the table cut to four.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Brentford 1-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Feb-12/brentford-1-1-arsenal-match-report|date=12 February 2026|access-date=14 February 2026|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arsenal followed through on all fronts, hosting League One club [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] in midweek for their tie in the FA Cup fourth round on 15 February. A first-half blitz which included a [[Jack Hunt (footballer)|Jack Hunt]] own goal and goals from Madueke, Martinelli, and Jesus, sent Arteta's men into the fifth round of the competition. 16-year-old Hale End product [[Marli Salmon]] made his home debut during the match, replacing Saliba just after the hour mark.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 4-0 Wigan Athletic|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Feb-15/arsenal-wigan-athletic-match-report|date=15 February 2026|access-date=15 February 2026|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref> Arsenal were later drawn to another League One club for the fifth round, [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mansfield Town drawn in FA Cup fifth round|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/mansfield-town-drawn-fa-cup-fifth-round|date=16 February 2026|access-date=16 February 2026|first=Arsenal|last=Media|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 18 February, Arsenal traveled to the West Midlands to face bottom of the table Wolves at the [[Molineux Stadium]]. In the fourth minute, Saka latched onto a perfect Rice cross, heading between the legs of [[José Sá]] to give the visitors an early advantage. The Gunners had two on 56 minutes, as Gabriel fed Hincapié who turned it high into the opposition net. [[Rob Edwards (footballer, born 1982)|Rob Edwards]]'s men weren't done yet, however, as Spaniard [[Hugo Bueno (footballer, born 2002)|Hugo Bueno]] lashed a top-corner screamer just five minutes later to halve the deficit. Deep into stoppage time, Raya spilled a cross which [[Tom Edozie]] collected. The 19-year-old debutant fired on the volley and was denied by the woodwork, only for a deflection off a desperate Calafiori to turn the ball back in past the goal line. The match ended 2–2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Wolverhampton Wanderers 2-2 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Feb-18/wolves-2-2-arsenal-match-report|date=18 February 2026|access-date=1 March 2026|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Arsenal succeeded this setback with a North London Derby away against Tottenham Hotspur on 22 February. Arteta opted for two attacking changes from the Wolves draw four days prior, with Eze and Trossard coming in for Ødegaard and Madueke. The Gunners began the game with intent, with both Saliba and Gyökeres squandering great chances. But they soon had a deserved lead as Saka squeezed past [[Djed Spence]] on the byline, firing a dangerous ball near the six-yard box which was converted by Eze. Tottenham responded quickly with [[Randal Kolo Muani]] pouncing on a complacent Rice and beating Raya on 34 minutes. The second half began with communication problems involving match officials, but it was Gyökeres who caused the biggest problems for the hosts once the interval got underway. The Swede took a touch from Timber's early cross before tucking an outstanding finish home to beat a flailing [[Guglielmo Vicario]]. Two became three with a scramble inside the Spurs penalty area, as flick-ons, blocks, and ricochets settled the ball nicely for Eze who made it five goals in two matches against Arsenal's North London rivals via a cool finish into an empty net. Gyökeres sealed the victory and another brace in added time, bending into the top-right corner to send his triumphant side five points clear at the league summit.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Tottenham Hotspur 1-4 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Feb-22/tottenham-hotspur-1-4-arsenal-match-report|date=1 March 2026|access-date=1 March 2026|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

===March===
{{football squad on pitch|align=right|flag_template=flagg2
| GK_nat = ESP | GK = Arizzabalaga
| RB_nat = ENG | RB = White
| RCB_nat = FRA | RCB = Saliba
| LCB_nat = BRA | LCB = Gabriel
| LB_nat = ECU | LB = Hincapié
| RCM_nat = ESP | RCM = Zubimendi
| LCM_nat = ENG | LCM = Rice
| SS_nat = GER | SS = Havertz 
| RW_nat = ENG | RW = Saka (c)
| LW_nat = BEL | LW = Trossard
| CF_nat = SWE | CF = Gyökeres 
| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1 formation]]) for EFL Cup Final against Manchester City on 22 March<ref>{{Cite web|title=Starting Lineups - Arsenal vs Man City |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-manchester-city/teams/553923|website=Sky Sports|date=22 March 2026 |access-date=5 April 2026}}</ref>}}
The Gunners kicked off a busy March with a home match against Chelsea, the two sides' fourth meeting of the season. Arteta's men emerged unchanged from their previous outing against Tottenham on 22 February, with no game for both sides during the midweek. The hosts started brightly and scored through Saliba, breaking the deadlock early on just like they had one week prior. Corresponding to the Spurs game, Arsenal shot themselves in the foot again as Hincapié flicked on [[Reece James]]'s corner into his own net to draw the game in first half stoppage time. Chelsea opened the second half with immense dominace, with the equaliser sucking the life out of the Emirates crowd and the home team. But just as the Gunners seemed to be losing their footing on the match, Timber nodded in a pinpoint Rice corner, securing a precious 2–1 lead. [[Pedro Neto]] was then shown a second a second yellow card for a sliding challenge on Martinelli, as Arsenal survived a late wave of pressure to secure all three points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-01/arsenal-2-1-chelsea-match-report|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=1 March 2026|date=1 March 2026}}</ref>

Arsenal played Brighton at a packed [[Amex Stadium]] on 4 March. Marking his 300th appearance for club, Saka's 9th minute goal allowed the visitors some early breathing space, as they sustained wave after wave of Brighton attacks. The ''Seagulls'' were looking likely to equalise, before the introductions of Havertz, Trossard, and Calafiori around the hour mark helped the Gunners secure another vital three points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Brighton 0-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-04/brighton-hove-albion-0-1-arsenal-match-report|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=8 March 2026|date=4 March 2026}}</ref>

Arteta's men then traveled away to [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]] on 7 March for the FA Cup 5th Round. A much-changed Arsenal side from the midweek fielded the likes of 16-year-olds Dowman and Salmon playing in an unusual 3-4-3 formation. Madueke and Martinelli, the only survivors from Wednesday's league clash, combined as the latter set up the former's superb first-time, outside-the-area finish. But just 5 minutes after halftime, Mansfield were level as [[Will Evans (footballer, born 1997)|Will Evans]] raced past Mosquera before beating Arizzabalaga at his near post. Substitute Eze then found himself in space on 66 minutes, striking into the top-right corner with immense power to send the Gunners to the quarter-finals of the competition for the first time since their winning run in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Mansfield Town 1-2 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-07/mansfield-town-1-2-arsenal-match-report|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=8 March 2026|date=7 March 2026}}</ref>

On 11 March, Arsenal travelled to Germany to face [[Bundesliga]] side [[Bayer Leverkusen]] in the Champions League [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|round of 16 first leg]]. On 19 minutes, Martinelli was fed by Gyökeres inside the box, with the Brazilian smashing his attempt off the crossbar. Hincapié, playing against his parent club, followed suit through a shot straight at Leverkusen goalkeeper [[Janis Blaswich]], who made a routine stop on the powerful effort. The home side took the lead shortly after the restart, as an unmarked [[Robert Andrich]] headed home from a corner, bypassing a napping Arsenal defence. The visitors ramped up the urgency following this setback, with Arteta sending Madueke and Havertz into the fray to change the momentum. Soon enough, these changes came to fruition as the England international drew a penalty in the 86th minute. Havertz  dispatched the spot-kick, leveling the tie against his boyhood club heading into the second leg at the Emirates.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Bayer Leverkusen 1-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-11/bayer-leverkusen-1-1-arsenal-match-report|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=15 March 2026|date=11 March 2026}}</ref>

Arsenal returned to the Emirates to play 8th position Everton  on 14 March. After a back-and-forth first hour which saw Everton winger [[Dwight McNeil]] denied by the post and an acrobatic block from Calafiori, Martinelli and Gyökeres were introduced to freshen things up in attack on 61 minutes. Dowman and Hincapié were brought on ten minutes later. In the 89th minute, the subs combined as Dowman supplied Hincapié a phenomenal cross, with the Ecuadorian defender chesting it down for Gyökeres to poke into an open goal. Deep into stoppage time, Dowman had his goal as the teenage sensation floored two defenders on a quick counter following a corner, carrying  the ball sixty-five yards to finish into an empty net. This goal meant that at just 16 years and 73 days, the [[Arsenal F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Hale End]] product had become the [[Premier League records and statistics#goalscoring|youngest goalscorer in Premier League history]], eclipsing [[James Vaughan (footballer, born 1988)|James Vaughan]]'s record by over half a year. The 2–0 win massively boosted the home side's title bid, propelling them ten points above a faltering Manchester City, who would draw away at West Ham United the following day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-0 Everton|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-14/arsenal-2-0-everton-match-report|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=21 March 2026|date=14 March 2026}}</ref>

Arsenal hosted Bayer Leverkusen in the second leg of the Champions League round of 16 on 17 March. Heading into the leg tied on aggregate with the German outfit, Arteta deployed a strong starting XI with only Timber missing out from injury. Gabriel, Trossard, and Saka squandered key chances early on, but these rued opportunities would be canceled out through a stunning top-corner volley on the turn by Eze. However, Arsenal's number 10 wouldn't be the only one to net a screamer in the match, as in the 74th minute, fellow countryman Rice controlled the ball nicely near the edge of the area before rolling an inch-perfect finish inside of the post. Late into the match, Raya added another stop to his growing catalogue of great saves, tipping away [[Christian Kofane]]'s stretched effort on 87 minutes. Having completed a 3–1 aggregate defeat of Leverkusen, Arteta's men could now look forward to their third Champions League quarter-final in a row, where they would play [[Sporting CP]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 2-0 Bayer Leverkusen (3-1)|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-17/arsenal-2-0-bayer-leverkusen-match-report|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=21 March 2026|date=17 March 2026}}</ref>

On 22 March, Arsenal traveled to [[Wembley Stadium]] to take on Manchester City in the [[2026 EFL Cup final]]. The match was Arsenal's first major cup final under Arteta since the [[2020 FA Cup final]], and a repeat of the [[2018 EFL Cup final]] where City beat Arsene Wenger's Gunners 3–0. Timber and Eze were the only major absentees for Arsenal, who were both out injured. Arteta also opted to play Arizzabalaga in goal instead of the usual Raya. Arsenal started the match the brighter of the two sides, with Zubimendi sending Havertz through on goal in the sixth minute, only for the German to fire straight at City goalkeeper [[James Trafford]]. As the game continued, however, Pep Guardiola's side enjoyed the greater share of possession, pinning Arteta's men in their own half. [[Erling Haaland]] squandered a great chance on the cusp of halftime, heading over under great pressure from White and Hincapié. After the break, City began wave after wave of relentless attacks, with [[Antoine Semenyo]] and [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] both firing wide. But just before the hour mark, the Sky Blue had their lead through [[Nico O'Reilly]], who headed into an empty net after goalkeeper Arrizabalaga spilled a cross. The young left-back soon doubled the advantage, as he lost his marker, Saka, before receiving [[Matheus Nunes]]'s cross and heading home again. Arteta's substitutions failed to spark a comeback, though Calafiori and Jesus both struck the woodwork late on. City's 2–0 triumph saw their name engraved onto the trophy for the ninth time, and a record fifth time for manager Pep Guardiola. It was Arsenal's first loss in seven meetings against the Manchester club since a 4–1 thrashing in April 2023. The defeat also ended hopes of an unprecedented quadruple for the Gunners, heading into the fourth and final international break of the campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-22/arsenal-0-2-manchester-city-match-report|title=Report: Arsenal 0-2 Manchester City|date=22 March 2026|access-date=27 March 2026|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

Thirteen Arsenal players (excluding loaned out players) were named in their respective countries' senior squads for international fixtures in March: Martinelli (Brazil), Nørgaard (Denmark), Hincapié (Ecuador), Madueke, Saka, Rice, and White (England), Havertz (Germany), Calafiori (Italy), Mosquera, Zubimendi, and Raya (Spain), and Gyökeres (Sweden).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/which-gunners-are-going-international-duty|title=Which Gunners are going on international duty?|date=24 March 2026|access-date=27 March 2026|first=Charlie|last=Peat|publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

===April===

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3 formation]]) for Champions League away match against Atletico Madrid on 29 April<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting Lineups - Atletico Madrid vs Arsenal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/atletico-madrid-vs-arsenal/teams/554947 |website=Sky Sports |date=29 April 2026 |access-date=29 April 2026}}</ref>}}
Arsenal began April with disappointment as their FA Cup journey came to an end following a 2–1 defeat away to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the quarter-finals on 4 April.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/southampton-2-1-arsenal-gunners-stunned-in-fa-cup-quarter-final-exit-42662097|title=Southampton 2-1 Arsenal, Gunners Stunned in FA Cup Quarter Final Exit|website=OneFootball|date=4 April 2026}}</ref> Arteta rotated heavily following the international break, but the hosts capitalised on defensive lapses to progress to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Roberts|first=Alex|url=https://www.tribalfootball.com/article/soccer-fa-cup-mikel-arteta-blames-unusual-defensive-mistakes-for-arsenal-s-shock-fa-cup-elimination-57fa6da6-005e-4e62-abbf-367e73382cb6|title=Mikel Arteta blames "unusual" defensive mistakes for Arsenal's shock FA Cup elimination|website=Tribal Football|date=4 April 2026}}</ref> After Gyökeres scored the equaliser in the second half, Southampton struck a late winner to eliminate Arsenal from the competition.<ref>{{cite web|last=Peat|first=Charlie|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Apr-04/southampton-arsenal-match-report|title=Report: Southampton 2-1 Arsenal|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=4 April 2026}}</ref> Three days later, the Gunners travelled to [[Lisbon]] for the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final against [[Sporting CP]]. In a tense and cagey affair, Arsenal secured a crucial 1–0 victory thanks to a composed stoppage-time finish from [[Kai Havertz]], assisted by [[Gabriel Martinelli]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Howell|first=Alex|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clyx8k8pn8dt|title=Sporting CP 0–1 Arsenal|website=BBC Sport|date=7 April 2026}}</ref>

Arsenal's momentum suffered another setback on 11 April as they fell to a shock 2–1 home defeat against [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/740908|title=Arsenal suffer huge PL title blow with home defeat to Bournemouth|website=ESPN|date=11 April 2026}}</ref> Despite Gyökeres scoring an equaliser from the penalty spot after an early setback, defensive mistakes and a lack of cutting edge allowed the visitors to restore their advantage in the second half, raising fresh questions in the Premier League title race.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arteta-we-were-far-our-standards|title=Arteta: 'We were far from our standards'|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=11 April 2026}}</ref> Arteta's side responded in Europe on 15 April, holding Sporting CP to a goalless draw at the Emirates Stadium to progress to the Champions League semi-finals with a 1–0 aggregate victory, securing consecutive semi-final appearances in the competition for the first time in the club's history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-mena/football/uefa-champions-league/articles-video/arsenal-survive-tense-sporting-stalemate-to-reach-champions-league-semis-2026-04-15|title=Arsenal survive tense Sporting stalemate to reach Champions League semis|website=beIN SPORTS|date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

The title race suffered another major blow four days later as Arsenal were defeated 2–1 away to Manchester City.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/epl-2026-manchester-city-defeat-arsenal-to-take-control-of-the-title-race-liverpool-win-first-merseyside-derby-at-evertons-new-stadium/news-story/d46df744e9827a291ac89b92d896ab0d |title=Arsenal hit title panic button as City smell blood; Spurs’ huge relegation blow — PL Wrap |publisher=FOX Sports |date=20 April 2026 }}</ref> Guardiola's side controlled much of the possession, with [[Rayan Cherki]] opening the scoring early on before Havertz capitalised on a pressing error by Donnarumma to equalise just two minutes later.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mendola |first=Nicholas |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/rayan-cherki-goal-video-vs-160900871.html |title=Rayan Cherki goal video vs Arsenal, Donnarumma error video, Havertz goal vs Man City |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=19 April 2026 }}</ref> However, Haaland restored City's lead in the second half, handing Arsenal a damaging defeat in the title race.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lee|first=Sam|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7220216/2026/04/23/man-city-top-premier-league-title/|title=How Manchester City climbed the mountain: From regaining control to the rise of Cherki|website=The Athletic|date=23 April 2026}}</ref> City later defeated [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] to move top of the table ahead of Arsenal on goal difference, with the two sides level on points.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dawson|first=Rob|url=https://global.espn.com/football/story/_/id/48564199/manchetser-city-go-top-table-title-race-fine-margins|title=Manchester City go top as Premier League title race reaches fine margins|website=ESPN|date=22 April 2026}}</ref>

Arsenal steadied themselves on 25 April with a hard-fought 1–0 victory over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. An early strike from Eze proved decisive in a physical contest, while Arsenal’s defence held firm to secure a valuable clean sheet in the closing stages.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c04x6p97vwzt|title=Arsenal 1–0 Newcastle United|website=BBC Sport|date=25 April 2026}}</ref> On 29 April, Arsenal travelled to Spain to face [[Atlético Madrid]] in the first leg of their Champions League semi-final. Gyökeres converted a penalty shortly before halftime to give Arsenal the lead, but Atlético responded in the second half through a [[Julián Álvarez]] penalty, as the match ended in a 1–1 draw at the [[Metropolitano Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/02a4-2081fa8b7112-8f4474ea29c4-1000--atleti-1-1-arsenal-highlights-viktor-gyokeres-and-julian-alv/|title=Atleti 1-1 Arsenal highlights: Viktor Gyökeres and Julián Alvarez on target in Champions League semi-final first leg|website=UEFA|date=29 April 2026}}</ref>

===May===
{{football squad on pitch|align=right|flag_template=flagg2
| GK_nat = ESP | GK = Raya
| RB_nat = ESP | RB = Mosquera
| RCB_nat = FRA | RCB = Saliba
| LCB_nat = BRA | LCB = Gabriel
| LB_nat = ECU | LB = Hincapié
| RCM_nat = ENG | RCM = Rice
| LCM_nat = ENG | LCM = Lewis-Skelly
| SS_nat = NOR | SS = Ødegaard (c)

| LW_nat = BEL | LW = Trossard

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1 formation]]) for Champions League Final against Paris Saint-Germain on 30 May<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 May 2026 |access-date=30 May 2026 |title=Starting Lineups - PSG vs Arsenal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/paris-saint-germain-vs-arsenal/teams/554950 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref>}}
Arsenal opened May with a commanding 3–0 home victory over [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], a result that further strengthened their position at the top of the table, moving them six points clear.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smyth|first=Rob|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/may/02/arsenal-v-fulham-premier-league-live|title=Arsenal have opened a six-point lead over Manchester City in the title race after a comprehensive home victory over Fulham|website=The Guardian|date=2 May 2026}}</ref> A brace from Gyökeres and one from Saka sealed a comfortable afternoon at the Emirates.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rogers|first=Jonathon|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-May-02/arsenal-3-0-fulham-match-report|title=Report: Arsenal 3-0 Fulham|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=2 May 2026}}</ref> Gyökeres' strikes also saw the Swedish forward reach over 20 goals in all competitions during his debut season, becoming the first Arsenal player to achieve the feat since [[Alexis Sánchez]] in [[2014–15 Arsenal F.C. season|2014–15]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rogers|first=Jonathon|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gyokeres-joins-elite-club-after-hitting-20-goals|title=Gyokeres joins elite club after hitting 20 goals|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=3 May 2026}}</ref> Title challengers Manchester City, meanwhile, only managed a 3–3 draw away to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], scoring a last-minute stoppage-time equaliser through [[Jérémy Doku]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Bate|first=Adam|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/13538623/everton-3-3-man-city-jeremy-doku-scored-a-97th-minute-equaliser-but-city-gift-arsenal-title-advantage-after-collapse|title=Everton 3-3 Man City: Jeremy Doku scored a 97th-minute equaliser but City gift Arsenal title advantage after collapse|website=Sky Sports|date=3 May 2026}}</ref> The result further boosted Arsenal's title chances, widening the gap at a crucial stage of the season despite Manchester City still having a game in hand.<ref>{{cite web|last=Braidwood|first=Jamie|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/sport/arsenal-man-city-premier-league-title-race-b2970560.html|title=How Arsenal could win the Premier League after Man City’s dramatic collapse against Everton|website=The Independent|date=5 May 2026}}</ref>

On 5 May, Arsenal hosted [[Atlético Madrid]] in the second leg of their Champions League semi-final tie. In a tense and tactical encounter, the breakthrough came through Saka, whose composed finish proved decisive in a 1–0 victory on the night.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/05/sport/live-news/champions-league-semifinal-atletico-madrid-arsenal|title=Arsenal defeats Atlético Madrid to book a place in the Champions League final for the first time in 20 years|website=CNN|date=5 May 2026}}</ref> That result secured Arsenal's passage to their second [[2026 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]] in 20 years, marking a significant milestone in Arteta's European project.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.sky.com/story/arsenal-reach-champions-league-final-for-the-first-time-in-20-years-13540566|title=Arsenal reach Champions League final for the first time in 20 years|website=Sky News|date=5 May 2026}}</ref> The unbeaten run to the final saw Arsenal record 11 wins and three draws from their 14 matches in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zakutskaja|first=Lera|url=https://tribuna.com/amp/en/news/2026-05-06-arsenal-secure-historic-champions-league-final-return-with-recordbreaking-unbeaten-run/|title=Arsenal secure historic Champions League final return with record-breaking unbeaten run|website=Tribuna.com|date=6 May 2026}}</ref> The club also conceded just six goals throughout their European campaign, while goalkeeper [[David Raya]] recorded his ninth clean sheet of the competition, equalling the Champions League record.<ref>{{cite web |last=Peat |first=Charlie |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/clean-sheet-record-inspiring-our-ucl-journey |title=The clean sheet record inspiring our UCL journey |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=6 May 2026 }}</ref> The win over Atlético also confirmed a historic statistical milestone for the club. Arsenal reached 41 wins across the season, matching their best-ever total from [[1970–71 Arsenal F.C. season|1970–71]], while their defensive record stood out with 30 clean sheets, the club's best return since [[1993–94 Arsenal F.C. season|1993–94]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/de/news/arsenal-equal-wins-and-clean-sheet-records-as-unbeaten-champions-league-run-reaches-14-42825369|title=Arsenal equal wins and clean sheet records as unbeaten Champions League run reaches 14|website=OneFootball|date=6 May 2026}}</ref>

On 10 May, Arsenal secured a 1–0 away victory over relegation-battling West Ham United, with [[Leandro Trossard]] scoring the only goal in the 83rd minute.<ref>{{cite web |last=McNulty |first=Phil |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crkpe566737t |title=West Ham United 0–1 Arsenal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=10 May 2026 }}</ref> The match featured late drama in stoppage time when [[Callum Wilson]] appeared to have equalised for West Ham, but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review ruled that [[Pablo (footballer, born 2004)|Pablo]] had committed a foul on Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya during the build-up, preserving Arsenal's lead and securing the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/west-ham-vs-arsenal-live-updates-premier-league-score-result/7500OWgj87YV/ |title=Arsenal poised for Premier League title after controversial VAR call earns tense win at West Ham: Live updates, reaction |publisher=The New York Times |date=10 May 2026 }}</ref> VAR decision, reviewed by referee [[Chris Kavanagh (referee)|Chris Kavanagh]] and advised by VAR official [[Darren England]], was later described as one of the most pivotal VAR calls in Premier League history, with the incident drawing widespread debate among refereeing analysts and commentators.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gardner |first=Jamie |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/west-ham-arsenal-chris-kavanagh-var-b2974305.html |title=West Ham-Arsenal referee and VAR praised for ‘really good teamwork’ after disallowed goal controversy |publisher=The Independent |date=11 May 2026 }}</ref>

On 18 May, Arsenal secured a 1–0 victory over Burnley, with Saka delivering a corner that was headed in by Havertz.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/arsenal-vs-burnley-live-updates-premier-league-score-result/IO7hE6DqW4Kr/ |title=How Arsenal moved within touching distance of Premier League title with win against Burnley |publisher=The New York Times |date=18 May 2026 }}</ref> The result marked Arsenal's 22nd different league match in which they scored from a set piece that season,<ref>{{cite web |last=Oludare |first=Shina |url=https://www.tribalfootball.com/article/soccer-premier-league-arsenal-break-own-premier-league-set-piece-record-vs-burnley-f1800799-9d37-49fe-a805-9ee2e0735852 |title=Arsenal break own Premier League set-piece record vs Burnley |publisher=Tribal Football |date=18 May 2026 }}</ref> as well as a joint-record sixth match in which they did not concede a single shot on target, matching their feat from the [[2003–04 Arsenal F.C. season|2003–04]] campaign.<ref>{{cite web |last=Knapton |first=Ben |url=https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/title-race/news/saka-emulates-henry-as-arsenal-equal-two-pl-records-in-burnley-success_597793.html |title=Arsenal equal two Premier League records as Bukayo Saka emulates Thierry Henry in Burnley victory |publisher=Sports Mole |date=18 May 2026 }}</ref> Raya also equaled the club record for most clean sheets in a single campaign with 19, matching [[David Seaman]] in the [[1993–94 Arsenal F.C. season|1993–94]] and [[1998–99 Arsenal F.C. season|1998–99]] seasons,<ref>{{cite web |last=Clarke |first=Adrian |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4604681/202526-premier-league-golden-glove-which-goalkeeper-has-kept-the-most-clean-sheets |title=Raya presented with Coca-Cola Golden Glove award |publisher=Premier League |date=18 May 2026 |access-date=19 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260518103450/https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4604681/202526-premier-league-golden-glove-which-goalkeeper-has-kept-the-most-clean-sheets |archive-date=18 May 2026 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/2026-05-19-david-raya-equals-arsenal-record-for-most-premier-league-clean-sheets-in-a-single-season/ |title=David Raya equals Arsenal record for most Premier League clean sheets in a single season |publisher=Tribuna.com |date=19 May 2026 }}</ref> while Saka became only the third Arsenal player after [[Thierry Henry]] and [[Dennis Bergkamp]] to register 50 goals and assists for the club.<ref>{{cite web |last=James |first=Josh |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/talking-points-our-big-win-against-burnley |title=Talking points from our big win against Burnley |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=18 May 2026 }}</ref> A day later, Arsenal secured their fourth Premier League title and their first since the 2003–04 season after second-place Manchester City were held to a 1–1 away draw by Bournemouth, leaving Arsenal four points clear with one match remaining.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/13545591/arsenal-win-premier-league-mikel-artetas-side-end-22-year-wait-for-title |title=Arsenal win Premier League: Mikel Arteta's side end 22-year wait for title |publisher=Sky Sports |date=19 May 2026 }}</ref> On the final day of the season, they secured a 2–1 away victory over Crystal Palace, after which captain Martin Ødegaard lifted the trophy for their 14th English league title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/video-martin-odegaard-lifts-premier-league-trophy-arsenal-celebrate-first-title-in-22-years-final-day-win-at-crystal-palace/blt8d20cb733f39dbec |title=VIDEO: Martin Odegaard lifts Premier League trophy as Arsenal celebrate first title in 22 years after final day win at Crystal Palace |publisher=Goal.com |date=24 May 2026 }}</ref> They also became the first team in Premier League history to complete a campaign without conceding a penalty or receiving a red card.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wright |first=Nick |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/13546939/crystal-palace-1-2-arsenal-champions-finish-historic-season-on-a-high-thanks-to-gabriel-jesus-and-noni-madueke-goals |title=Crystal Palace 1-2 Arsenal: Champions finish historic season on a high thanks to Gabriel Jesus and Noni Madueke goals |publisher=Sky Sports |date=24 May 2026 }}</ref> Arsenal's triumph was built on defensive resilience and set-piece dominance throughout the campaign, finishing the season as the league's best defensive side while also scoring 18 goals from corners at a historic rate.<ref>{{cite web |last=O'Hanlon |first=Ryan |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48838211/9-stats-explain-how-arsenal-won-premier-league |title=9 stats that explain how Arsenal won the Premier League |publisher=ESPN |date=23 May 2026 }}</ref>

On 30 May, Arsenal contested their second UEFA Champions League final against defending champions [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]]. The Gunners took an early lead through Kai Havertz and maintained their advantage for the first half. However, their lead was cancelled out in the second half when [[Cristhian Mosquera]] conceded a penalty after fouling [[Khvicha Kvaratskhelia]], allowing [[Ousmane Dembélé]] to equalise from the spot.<ref>{{cite web |last=Marsh |first=Charlotte |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/paris-saint-germain-vs-arsenal/report/554950 |title=PSG 1-1 Arsenal (PSG win 4-3 on penalties): Gunners heartbreak in Champions League final as Paris Saint-Germain win in Budapest |publisher=Sky Sports |date=30 May 2026 }}</ref> With neither side able to find a winner, the match was decided by a penalty shootout, where Paris Saint-Germain prevailed 4–3, extending Arsenal's wait for a first European Cup title and leaving them as the competition's most-played club never to win it (226 matches).<ref>{{cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-May-30/paris-saint-germain-1-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: PSG 1-1 Arsenal (AET, 4-3 pens) |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=30 May 2026 }}</ref>

* ''Player''<sup>†</sup> – Player who departed Arsenal permanently or on loan during the season.
* Player (''HG'') – Player who fulfils the Premier League's "[[Homegrown Player Rule (England)|Home Grown Player]]" criteria.<ref name="squad lists (Feb) PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4243590 |title=2024/25 Updated Premier League squad lists |date=7 Feb 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="PL squad AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-submit-202425-premier-league-squad-list |title=Arsenal submit 2024/25 Premier League squad list |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=13 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref>
* Player (''CT'') – Player who fulfils UEFA's "[[Homegrown Player Rule (UEFA)|club-trained player]]" criteria.<ref name="Regulations of UCL">{{cite web |url=https://documents.uefa.com/r/Regulations-of-the-UEFA-Champions-League-2025/26/Article-31-Player-lists-Online |title=Article 31 Player lists • Regulations of the UEFA Champions League (Edition: 2025/26) |date=1 Mar 2025 |website=[[UEFA]] |access-date=5 May 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523032208/https://documents.uefa.com/r/Regulations-of-the-UEFA-Champions-League-2025/26/Article-31-Player-lists-Online |archive-date=23 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="Regulations of UCL PDF">{{cite web |url=https://documents.uefa.com/api/khub/maps/FKQL5fz2x9xSknAq1daySg/attachments/tx0Zgcv_vWdWa2N_o6rmQw-FKQL5fz2x9xSknAq1daySg/content |title=Regulations of the UEFA Champions League (Edition: 2024/25) |date=1 Mar 2025 |website=UEFA |format=PDF |pages=32–35 |access-date=5 May 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523032613/https://documents.uefa.com/api/khub/maps/FKQL5fz2x9xSknAq1daySg/attachments/tx0Zgcv_vWdWa2N_o6rmQw-FKQL5fz2x9xSknAq1daySg/content |archive-date=23 May 2025}}</ref>

==Academy==
===Academy coaching staff===
On 4 July 2025, Under-21s Head Coach Mehmet Ali departed the club to take up an Assistant coaching role at [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]].<ref name="Mehmet Ali departed AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/mehmet-ali-departs-brentford |title=Mehmet Ali departs for Brentford |date=4 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 Jul 2025}}</ref> Whilst it was initially on an interim basis, [[Max Porter (footballer)|Max Porter]] subsequently replaced Ali on a permanent basis on 15 August 2025. [[Ken Gillard]] became his assistant coach.<ref name="Max Porter named U21 Head Coach AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/max-porter-becomes-under-21s-head-coach |title=Max Porter becomes under-21s Head Coach |date=15 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=15 Aug 2025}}</ref>

==Board and management team==

On 19 September, the club announced a number of changes at board level, which included the departure of Executive Vice-chair Tim Lewis and the promotion of Richard Garlick from managing director to [[chief executive officer]]. Members of [[Kroenke Sports & Entertainment]] (KSE), Kelly Blaha and Otto Maly, long-term KSE advisor, Dave Steiner, and film producer and director, Ben Winston, a season ticket holder at Arsenal for over 30 years, all joined the board as non-executive directors.<ref name="Arsenal Board update AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-announces-leadership-and-board-update |title=Arsenal announces leadership and board update |date=19 Sep 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=19 Sep 2025}}</ref> The departure of Lewis, who has advised the KSE group since 2007 (including around the incremental purchase of Arsenal Football Club) and held a position at Arsenal since 2020 (thus steering the club through the financial peril of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]), was seen as a shock move.<ref name="Arsenal Board update NYTimes">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6618741/2025/09/19/arsenal-tim-lewis-leave-position/ |title=Tim Lewis to leave position as Arsenal executive vice-chair |last=Ornstein |first=David |date=19 Sep 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=19 Sep 2025}}</ref>

===Kit information===
This is Adidas's seventh year supplying Arsenal kit, having taken over from [[Puma (brand)|Puma]] at the beginning of the [[2019–20 Arsenal F.C. season|2019–20]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/adidas-partnership-extended-2030 |title=adidas partnership extended to 2030 |date=30 Sep 2022 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.adidas.com/football/adidas-and-arsenal-launch-new-partnership-with-2019-20-home-kit/s/a792ee1b-7f39-4f66-a095-a689e151ec5b |title=adidas and Arsenal launch new partnership with 2019/20 home kit |date=1 Jul 2019 |website=Adidas |access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref>

*'''Home:''' The club revealed their new home kit for the 2025–26 season on 15 May 2025. The kit uses Arsenal's traditional colours of red and white. The shirt has a red body and white sleeves and is complemented by white shorts and red socks. Red shorts may be used in some away games when there will be a colour clash with the home team's kit. Taken from the "Victoria Concordia Crescit" club [[Arsenal F.C.#Crest|crest]], first used in the [[1949–50 Arsenal F.C. season|1949–50]] season, the gothic "A" of "Arsenal" is repeated across the body of the shirt.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/details-behind-our-202526-adidas-home-kit |title=The details behind our 2025/26 adidas home kit |date=15 May 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=6 Jun 2025}}</ref> The kit was launched alongside a film named ''The pulse of our club''.<ref>{{cite AV media |title=The pulse of our club {{pipe}} Introducing the 25/26 adidas Football Home Kit |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rxe0-TnESDs |date=15 May 2024 |access-date=6 Jun 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}}</ref>
*'''Away:''' On 21 July, the Gunners released their new away kit, which is a tribute to the ability of the club's supporters to energise the players in to feeling "100ft tall", stand out and own the moment.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-launch-new-adidas-202526-away-kit |title=Arsenal launch new adidas 2025/26 away kit |date=21 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=21 Jul 2025}}</ref> The shirt has a dark navy base with a lighter-navy lightning bolt pattern, a signature away-kit design that was inspired by the [[Royal Arsenal Gatehouse]] lightning bolt.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/learn-about-inspiration-our-2526-away-kit |title=Learn about the inspiration for our 25/26 away kit |date=21 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=21 Jul 2025}}</ref> The kit is complemented by navy shorts and socks, whereby metallic grey shorts will be used in the away games in which there are a colour clash with the home team's kit. The kit was launched with an accompanying video named ''Ready for new heights''.<ref>{{cite AV media |title=Ready for new heights. {{pipe}} Introducing the 25/26 adidas Football Away Kit |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l6Pu2WPuknQ |date=21 Jul 2025 |access-date=21 Jul 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}}</ref>
*'''Third:''' On 4 August, the club released their new third kit, which is inspired by the 20th anniversary of Arsenal's final season at the "iconic" [[Arsenal Stadium|Highbury Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-launch-new-adidas-202526-third-kit |title=Arsenal launch new adidas 2025/26 third kit |date=4 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 Aug 2025}}</ref> The shirt has a white base with off-white details that echo the stadium's distinctive art deco architecture. It also features a polo collar with dark red and gold stripes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/inspiration-and-details-our-2526-third-kit |title=The inspiration and details on our 25/26 third kit |date=4 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 Aug 2025}}</ref> The kit is complemented by dark red shorts and white socks, whereby white shorts will be used in the away games in which there are a colour clash with the home team's kit. The kit was launched with an accompanying video named ''A tribute to elegance, art and style''.<ref>{{cite AV media |title=A tribute to elegance, art and style &#x2728;&#xFE0F; {{pipe}} Introducing the 25/26 adidas Football Third Kit |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v9wUsq1vyM4 |date=4 Aug 2025 |access-date=4 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}}</ref>
*'''Goalkeeper:''' The new goalkeeper kits are based on Adidas's goalkeeper template for the season.

==Pre-season and friendlies==
<!-- Update sources: https://www.arsenal.com/fixtures & https://www.arsenal.com/results -->
On 31 March 2025, Arsenal announced that they would travel to [[Hong Kong]] for the first time since [[2012–13 Arsenal F.C. season#Pre-season and friendlies|2012]] to partake in the first [[North London derby]] on international soil in the history of the fixture. The match took place in the recently opened [[Kai Tak Sports Park]] on 31 July.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-play-tottenham-hong-kong-july |title=Arsenal to play Tottenham in Hong Kong in July |date=31 Mar 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="First foreign NLD"/> On 11 April, Arsenal announced that they would be travelling to [[Singapore]] for the first time since [[2018–19 Arsenal F.C. season#Pre-season and friendlies|2018]] to play matches against [[Serie A|Italian]] side [[AC Milan]] and fellow [[Premier League]] side [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. The matches took place on 23 and 27 July respectively at the [[National Stadium, Singapore|National Stadium]], and finalised the club's three-match Asian pre-season schedule.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-play-ac-milan-newcastle-singapore |title=Arsenal to play AC Milan & Newcastle in Singapore |date=11 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref> On 5 July 2025, Arsenal announced that the concluding fixtures of the pre-season schedule would feature an [[Emirates Cup]] game against [[Athletic Bilbao]] on 9 August 2025 and a friendly three days earlier against fellow [[La Liga|Spanish]] side [[Villareal CF|Villareal]], both at the [[Emirates Stadium]].<ref name="Villarreal and Bilbao Friendlies"/>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2025–26 FA Cup}}

As a Premier League side, Arsenal entered the FA Cup in the third round, and were drawn away to [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal to play Portsmouth in FA Cup third round |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/fa-cup-third-round-draw-made |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=8 Dec 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=11 Dec 2025}}</ref> They were then drawn consecutive ties against [[EFL League One|League One]] opposition, hosting [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] in the fourth round<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal to play Wigan in FA Cup fourth round |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-discover-fa-cup-fourth-round-opponents |date=12 Jan 2026 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=12 Jan 2026}}</ref> and travelling to [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]] in the fifth round.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mansfield Town drawn in FA Cup fifth round |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/mansfield-town-drawn-fa-cup-fifth-round |date=16 Feb 2026 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=16 Feb 2026}}</ref> The club were then drawn to travel to their second Championship south coast tie of the competition at [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the quarter final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal draw Southampton in FA Cup quarter-finals |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-draw-southampton-fa-cup-quarter-finals |last=Peat |first=Charlie |date=9 Mar 2026 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=11 Mar 2026}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2025–26 EFL Cup}}

The Gunners entered the EFL Cup in the third round as one of the Premier League teams participating in UEFA competitions. As a seeded team, they were drawn [[Vale Park|away]] to [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/carabao-cup-third-round-opponents-confirmed |title=Port Vale drawn in Carabao Cup third round |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=27 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=27 Aug 2025}}</ref> They were then drawn consecutive home ties against Premier League opposition, with [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] in the fourth round<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/carabao-cup-fourth-round-opponents-drawn |title=Brighton drawn in Carabao Cup fourth round |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=24 Sep 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=25 Sep 2025}}</ref> and [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brighton drawn in Carabao Cup fourth round |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/carabao-cup-quarter-final-draw-made |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=29 Oct 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=30 Oct 2025}}</ref> The semi-final draw then pitted Arsenal against another London [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|rival]] in the form of [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], with the second and decisive leg taking place at home.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup semi-final draw made |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/carabao-cup-semi-final-draw-made |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=17 Dec 2025 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=21 Dec 2025}}</ref> In the [[2026 EFL Cup final|final]], the club lost to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-face-man-city-carabao-cup-final |title=Arsenal to face Man City in Carabao Cup final |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=4 Feb 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 Feb 2026}}</ref>

===UEFA Champions League===
{{main|2025–26 UEFA Champions League}}

====League phase====
{{main|2025–26 UEFA Champions League league phase}}

Arsenal's [[UEFA coefficient#Men's club coefficient|UEFA club coefficient]] was 98.000 points at the end of the previous campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/uefarankings/club/?year=2025 |title=Club coefficients {{pipe}} UEFA rankings |date=3 Jun 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=3 Jun 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607095234/https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/uefarankings/club/?year=2025 |archive-date=7 Jun 2025}}</ref> They were in Pot 2 for the league phase draw, which was held on 28 August 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/029c-1e954c3512ef-8b9c6fa0f83b-1000--champions-league-league-phase-draw-pots-confirmed/ |title=Champions League: League phase draw pots confirmed |date=28 Aug 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=28 Aug 2025}}</ref> Arsenal were randomly drawn to play [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] and [[Inter Milan]] (for the second consecutive season) from Pot 1, [[Atlético Madrid]] and [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] from Pot 2, [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] and [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]] from Pot 3, and finally debutant [[FC Kairat|Kairat]] and [[Athletic Bilbao]] from Pot 4.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/champions-league-league-phase-draw-made |title=Champions League league phase draw made |date=28 Aug 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=28 Aug 2025}}</ref>

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2025–26 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}

=====Round of 16=====
As a result of finishing first in the league phase, Arsenal were seeded for the round of 16 draw, which took take place on 27 February 2026, and played the second leg at home. They were drawn against German side [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] for the first time since [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League second group stage#Group D|2002]].<ref name="UCL knockout draw AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/bayer-leverkusen-drawn-champions-league-last-16 |title=Bayer Leverkusen drawn in Champions League last 16 |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=27 Feb 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=27 Feb 2026}}</ref>

=====Quarter-final=====
The draw for the quarter-final was automatically determined after the round of 16 draw on 27 February 2026. As a result of [[Sporting CP]] overcoming a three-goal deficit from their first leg against [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]], Arsenal were drawn to play the [[Primeira Liga|Portuguese]] [[2024–25 Primeira Liga#League table|champions]] for the third time in the past four European campaigns. As a result of their higher seeding, the club played the second leg at home.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/who-will-arsenal-face-ucl-quarter-finals |title=Who will Arsenal face in the UCL quarter-finals? |last=Peat |first=Charlie |date=17 Mar 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=17 Mar 2026}}</ref>

=====Semi-final=====
The draw for the semi-final was automatically determined after the quarter-final draw on 27 February 2026. Arsenal faced [[Atlético Madrid]] for the second time in the competition (after a 4–0 home win in the League Phase), as a result of their defeat of [[La Liga|Spanish]] rivals [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] 3–2 on aggregate in the previous round. Due to their higher seeding, the club once again played their second leg at home.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/dates-confirmed-champions-league-semi-final |title=Dates confirmed for Champions League semi-final |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=15 Apr 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=5 May 2026}}</ref>

=====Final=====
{{main article|2026 UEFA Champions League final}}
Having progressed past [[Atlético Madrid]] in the semi-finals, Arsenal reached only their second UEFA Champions League final in their history, having first done so in [[2006 UEFA Champions League final|2006]]. The club was seeking to win Europe's premier competition for the first time in their history and become the first team to play 14 or more matches in a single campaign and remain unbeaten.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-reach-202526-champions-league-final |title=Arsenal reach 2025/26 Champions League final |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=5 May 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=6 May 2026}}</ref> The Gunners faced [[2025 UEFA Champions League final|holders]] [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] for the second consecutive campaign, after the Parisians knocked the club out at the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League#Semi-finals|semi-final]] stage in the previous season. Arsenal would lose 4–3 on penalties following a 1–1 draw after regulation.
